paras.en: The looming battle with Suno will raise untested legal questions about the extent to which AI companies can be sued for allegedly ripping off a musical artist’s identity. The use of AI to convincingly mimic real people has been one of the booming technology’s most controversial applications, and no where less so than an industry largely built on famous singing voices.
paras.zh: 与 Suno 迫在眉睫的战斗将引发未经检验的法律问题，即人工智能公司在多大程度上可以因涉嫌盗用音乐艺术家的身份而被起诉。使用人工智能令人信服地模仿真人一直是蓬勃发展的技术中最具争议性的应用之一，而且与一个主要建立在著名歌声基础上的行业同样如此。

paras.en: “Elvis’ voice possessed a distinctively rich vocal timbre, with a warm velvety resonance and perfectly employed vibrato, coupled with his ability to vary his technique and delivery within the same song as well as across several different styles of music, which became his immediately recognizable musical signature across the world,” the lawsuit says.
paras.zh: 诉讼称：“埃尔维斯的声音拥有独特丰富的音色、温暖柔和的共鸣和完美运用的颤音，再加上他在同一首歌以及多种不同风格的音乐中改变技巧和表达的能力，这成为他在世界各地立即被识别的音乐标志。”

paras.en: Suno has argued in other lawsuits that its current models do not allow users to include the names of specific artists in prompts, nor produce outputs that mimic specific real voices. But in Friday’s complaint, the Elvis owners say those claims are “unequivocally false.” They included links to videos capturing the use of Suno’s platform to play songs that sound remarkably similar to Presley.
paras.zh: Suno 在其他诉讼中辩称，其当前模型不允许用户在提示中包含特定艺术家的姓名，也不允许生成模仿特定真实声音的输出。但在周五的投诉中，猫王所有者表示这些说法“毫无疑问是错误的”。其中包含视频链接，这些视频捕捉到如何使用 Suno 的平台来播放听起来与普雷斯利非常相似的歌曲。

paras.en: “Those … are NOT examples of Elvis Presley singing. They are synthetic and unlicensed uses of Elvis’ voice and likeness,” Busch writes. “There are hundreds to thousands more like it.”
paras.zh: “这些……不是猫王歌唱的例子。它们是对猫王声音和肖像的合成和未经许可的使用，”布希写道。 “类似的还有成百上千个。”

paras.en: “Suno is the embodiment of why the ELVIS Act was so essentially required,” the lawsuit reads. “Suno has stolen Elvis’ voice, his image, and likeness, as well as his copyrighted works on, literally, a breathtaking scale, and must now be called to answer for its theft.”
paras.zh: 诉讼中写道：“Suno 体现了为什么 ELVIS 法案如此重要。” “苏诺窃取了埃尔维斯的声音、他的形象和肖像，以及他的版权作品，其规模之大令人震惊，现在必须被要求为其盗窃行为负责。”

paras.en: Suno’s lawyers have argued such claims won’t hold up in court. In an earlier likeness case filed by Jason Isbell and other artists, the AI firm’s lawyers argued it merely uses artist names as “shorthand for the genre they perform in” and does not allow for direct theft of their voices. But the new lawsuit says that as recently as last month, Suno generated an Elvis clone based simply on lyrics that included his name.
paras.zh: 苏诺的律师辩称，这种说法在法庭上站不住脚。在杰森·伊斯贝尔（Jason Isbell）和其他艺术家早些时候提起的相似案件中，这家人工智能公司的律师辩称，它只是使用艺术家的名字作为“他们所表演的流派的简写”，并且不允许直接窃取他们的声音。但新的诉讼称，就在上个月，苏诺仅根据包含他名字的歌词生成了猫王克隆版。

paras.en: “Entering a musician’s name into Suno’s ‘Create’ function, such as Elvis’, causes Suno to generate unauthorized output based on his [name, image and likeness], which copies and reproduces the signature and recognizable aspects of his distinguished voice,” Busch writes in the new case.
paras.zh: “在 Suno 的‘创建’功能中输入音乐家的名字，例如猫王，会导致 Suno 根据他的[姓名、图像和肖像]生成未经授权的输出，从而复制和复制他杰出声音的签名和可识别方面，”Busch 在新案例中写道。

paras.en: In addition to the new voice claims, the lawsuit echoes the same accusations made against Anthropic over training on copyrighted Elvis songs, including “Can’t Help Falling in Love,” arguably Presley’s most famous track; “Don’t Be Cruel,” one of his early massive hits; and “A Little Less Conversation,” “All Shook Up,” “Return to Sender” and “(You’re the) Devil in Disguise”. And like the earlier case, the new lawsuit claims Suno stole those songs in order to replace human artists.
paras.zh: 除了新的声音主张之外，这起诉讼还呼应了针对 Anthropic 对猫王版权歌曲进行培训的同样指控，其中包括“Can't Help Falling in Love”，可以说是普雷斯利最著名的歌曲； 《Don’t Be Cruel》是他早期的热门歌曲之一；以及“少一点对话”、“一切都震惊了”、“返回发件人”和“（你是）伪装的魔鬼”。与之前的案件一样，新的诉讼声称苏诺窃取了这些歌曲以取代人类艺术家。

paras.en: “The next Elvis won’t pick up a guitar,” the Presley Enterprises lawyers write. “Suno’s ravenous race to the bottom aims to make human creativity obsolete, coldly replicating without a license in seconds what takes years to learn, struggle with, maintain, and endlessly attempt to make better and perfect.”
paras.zh: “下一个猫王不会拿起吉他，”普雷斯利企业的律师写道。 “Suno 贪婪的逐底竞赛旨在让人类的创造力变得过时，在没有许可的情况下在几秒钟内冷酷地复制需要数年时间学习、奋斗、维护并不断尝试变得更好和完美的东西。”

paras.en: Separately on Friday, the same attorneys another case against Suno on behalf of Eight Mile Style, a publisher that owns much of Eminem’s catalog. That case includes similar copyright allegations as the Elvis case, accusing the lab of training its models on the rapper’s “Lose Yourself,” “Without Me,” “Till I Collapse,” “The Real Slim Shady, “Stan” and other hits.
paras.zh: 周五，同一位律师代表八英里风格公司（Eight Mile Style）对苏诺提起另一起诉讼，该出版商拥有阿姆的大部分目录。该案包括与猫王案类似的版权指控，指控实验室根据说唱歌手的“Lose Yourself”、“Without Me”、“Till I Collapse”、“The Real Slim Shady”、“Stan”等热门歌曲来训练其模型。

paras.en: The Elvis and Eminem cases add to mounting legal challenges for Suno. The company was first sued in 2024 by all three major music companies over AI training. Though it settled with Warner Music Group last year and has vowed to partner with the music industry, is still litigating with UMG and Sony Music — who have shown no interest in striking a deal. It has also faced new cases in recent months from music publishers Round Hill Music and Reservoir, as well as the Isbell case over likenesses.
paras.zh: 埃尔维斯和埃米纳姆的案件给苏诺带来了日益严峻的法律挑战。该公司于 2024 年首次因人工智能培训问题被三大音乐公司起诉。尽管该公司去年与华纳音乐集团达成和解，并誓言要与音乐行业合作，但仍在与环球音乐集团和索尼音乐提起诉讼，而后者并没有表现出达成交易的兴趣。近几个月来，它还面临着来自音乐出版商 Round Hill Music and Reservoir 的新案件，以及 Isbell 的相似案件。

articles.title: ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Barrels Toward Historic $32M Box Office Launch With ‘Cat in the Hat’ at No. 2
articles.author: Ryan Gajewski

paras.en: Godzilla Minus Zero is king of the box office in its opening weekend as the sequel feature looks to dominate the frame that also sees the debuts of The Cat in the Hat, Ramayana, Wild Horse Nine and Club Kid.
paras.zh: 《哥斯拉减零》在首映周末成为票房之王，续集看起来将占据主导地位，而《戴帽子的猫》、《罗摩衍那》、《野马九号》和《俱乐部小子》也首次亮相。

paras.en: Hitting 3,254 North American theaters from GKids and Toho, Godzilla Minus Zero conquered $14.5 million on Friday, including Thursday previews, as it heads toward an estimated $32 million for the weekend. This is being touted as the highest-grossing live-action foreign-language opening at the box office since 2004’s Hero launched with $17.8 million. (It’s behind the debut of last year’s animated Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle with $70.6 million, while 2004’s The Passion of the Christ and its massive $83.8 million opening is not included in the category as an American-produced project). Filmmaker Takashi Yamazaki‘s sequel to 2023’s Oscar-winning Godzilla Minus One earned an A CinemaScore from audiences and is performing far above the distributor’s projected opening in the mid-$20 millions.
paras.zh: 《哥斯拉减零》周五在 GKids 和 Toho 的 3,254 家北美影院上映，包括周四的预映在内，票房收入为 1,450 万美元，预计周末票房将达到 3,200 万美元。该片被誉为自 2004 年《英雄》上映以来票房收入最高的真人外语片，票房收入为 1780 万美元。 （去年动画《鬼灭之刃：无限城堡》的首映票房为 7,060 万美元，而 2004 年的《耶稣受难记》首映票房高达 8,380 万美元，却没有被列为美国制作的影片）。电影制片人山崎隆制作的 2023 年奥斯卡获奖影片《哥斯拉减一》的续集获得了观众的 CinemaScore 评分，其表现远远高于发行商预计的 2000 万美元的首映票房。

paras.en: Ryunosuke Kamiki, Minami Hamabe and Min Tanaka star in the new movie that carries a reported budget in the mid-teens. It centers on postwar Japan dealing with attacks from the three-headed Ghidorah and the possibility of Godzilla’s return. Godzilla Minus Zero holds an impressive 90 percent critics approval on Rotten Tomatoes, with The Hollywood Reporter chief film critic David Rooney calling it a “thrilling jolt of marauding monster action.”
paras.zh: 这部新电影由神木龙之介、滨边南和田中敏主演，据报道，该电影的预算为十几岁。它以战后日本应对三头基多拉的攻击以及哥斯拉回归的可能性为中心。 《哥斯拉减零》在烂番茄上获得了高达 90% 的影评人认可，《好莱坞报道》首席影评人大卫·鲁尼称其为“惊心动魄的掠夺怪物动作片”。

paras.en: The sequel is making an even bigger footprint than Godzilla Minus One, which opened in December 2023 with $11.4 million domestically and reached $57.1 million for the run, adding $56.9 million internationally. The film rode its massive breakout success to become Japan’s first feature to win the best visual effects Oscar.
paras.zh: 这部续集的票房收入甚至比《哥斯拉减一》还要大，后者于 2023 年 12 月上映，国内票房为 1,140 万美元，首映票房达到 5,710 万美元，国际票房为 5,690 万美元。这部电影取得了巨大的突破性成功，成为日本第一部赢得奥斯卡最佳视觉效果奖的故事片。

paras.en: Warner Bros.’ The Cat in the Hat grossed $6 million domestically from 4,003 North American locations on Friday, including Thursday previews, and it is set to pounce on around $18 million for its opening frame. The studio had projected that the $92 million-budgeted film, which earned an A CinemaScore, would open with $20 million and hopes for word of mouth to help it play through the Thanksgiving holiday and into December.
paras.zh: 华纳兄弟出品的《戴帽子的猫》周五在北美 4,003 个外景地获得了 600 万美元的票房（包括周四的预映），预计首映票房将达到 1,800 万美元左右。该工作室预计这部预算为 9200 万美元、获得 CinemaScore 评分的电影首映票房为 2000 万美元，并希望通过口碑传播帮助其在感恩节假期和 12 月期间上映。

paras.en: Directors Erica Rivinoja and Alessandro Carloni’s animated adaptation of Dr. Seuss’ classic 1957 children’s book centers on the titular feline being given a final chance to prove his worth by helping a pair of siblings. Bill Hader leads the voice cast that also includes Matt Berry, Quinta Brunson and Xochitl Gomez. The movie marks Warner Bros. Pictures Animation’s first title since Bill Damaschke took over as president and chief creative officer in 2023.
paras.zh: 导演艾丽卡·里维诺贾 (Erica Rivinoja) 和亚历山德罗·卡罗尼 (Alessandro Carloni) 改编自苏斯博士 1957 年的经典儿童读物，讲述了这只同名猫得到了最后一次机会，通过帮助一对兄弟姐妹来证明自己的价值。比尔·哈德尔 (Bill Hader) 领衔配音，其他演员还包括马特·贝瑞 (Matt Berry)、昆塔·布伦森 (Quinta Brunson) 和索奇特尔·戈麦斯 (Xochitl Gomez)。这部电影是华纳兄弟动画公司自 2023 年比尔·达马施克 (Bill Damaschke) 接任总裁兼首席创意官以来的首部作品。

paras.en: Critics have been a bit aloof on the film, as it holds a 45 percent Rotten Tomatoes score from reviewers, with THR critic Frank Scheck calling it “more taxing than enjoyable.” It’s certainly getting better notices than Universal’s 2003 live-action The Cat in the Hat starring Mike Myers, which holds an 11 score on Rotten Tomatoes. That movie opened to $38.3 million domestically en route to a North American cume of $101 million against a $109 million budget.
paras.zh: 影评人对这部电影有点冷漠，因为它在烂番茄上的评分为 45%，THR 影评人弗兰克·谢克 (Frank Scheck) 称这部电影“更费力，而不是令人愉快”。毫无疑问，它比环球影业 2003 年由迈克·梅尔斯 (Mike Myers) 主演的真人版《戴帽子的猫》更受关注，该片在烂番茄上获得了 11 分。该片国内首映票房为 3830 万美元，北美票房为 1.01 亿美元，而预算为 1.09 亿美元。

paras.en: Sony Pictures releases Prime Focus Studios’ Ramayana: Rise of a Legend in 1,433 North American locations, with the film grossing $2.4 million Friday and headed to a sum of roughly $7.3 million for the weekend. Boasting the widest domestic launch ever for an Indian movie, director Nitesh Tiwari’s religious epic focuses on the life of Prince Rama, with the two-film project’s budget reported at $420 million and beyond. It holds a 76 score from critics on Rotten Tomatoes, along with an 89 from audiences.
paras.zh: 索尼影业 (Sony Pictures) 在北美 1,433 个影院上映了 Prime Focus Studios 的《罗摩衍那：传奇崛起》，该片周五票房收入 240 万美元，周末票房收入约为 730 万美元。导演尼泰什·蒂瓦里 (Nitesh Tiwari) 执导的这部宗教史诗片以拉玛王子的一生为主题，是迄今为止在印度国内上映最广泛的电影，两部电影项目的预算据报道高达 4.2 亿美元甚至更多。烂番茄影评人给该片打出了 76 分，观众给了 89 分。

paras.en: Also likely debuting in the top five is Angel Studios’ Drummer Boy, with directors Ben and Joel David Smallbone’s historical drama grossing $3.5 million Friday from 2,850 North American locations for a weekend opening around $7.9 million. Earning an A CinemaScore, the faith-based movie focuses on an unlikely bond during the American Revolution and stars Joel David Smallbone in the title role. On Rotten Tomatoes, it has a 50 critics score and a 93 from audiences.
paras.zh: 首次跻身前五名的还有 Angel Studios 的《鼓手男孩》，导演本·大卫·斯莫尔博恩 (Ben David Smallbone) 和乔尔·大卫·斯莫尔博恩 (Joel David Smallbone) 执导的历史剧周五在北美 2,850 家影院上映，票房收入 350 万美元，周末首映票房约为 790 万美元。这部以信仰为主题的电影获得了 A CinemaScore 评分，聚焦于美国独立战争期间一段看似不太可能的纽带，由乔尔·大卫·斯莫尔博恩 (Joel David Smallbone) 主演。在烂番茄上，它的评论家评分为 50 分，观众评分为 93 分。

paras.en: Academy Awards hopeful Wild Horse Nine opened in 1,100 North American theaters with around $2.4 million Friday for an estimated frame of $5.5 million. John Malkovich, Sam Rockwell and Steve Buscemi lead writer-director Martin McDonagh’s comedic thriller about two CIA operatives who travel from Santiago, Chile, to Easter Island in 1973. The Searchlight Pictures release holds a 94 critics score on Rotten Tomatoes, with Rooney’s review describing it as “uniquely affecting.”
paras.zh: 有望获得奥斯卡奖的《野马九人》周五在北美 1,100 家影院上映，票房约为 240 万美元，预计票房 550 万美元。约翰·马尔科维奇、山姆·洛克威尔和史蒂夫·布西密领衔编剧兼导演马丁·麦克唐纳这部喜剧惊悚片讲述了 1973 年两名中央情报局特工从智利圣地亚哥前往复活节岛的故事。探照灯影业发行的影片在烂番茄上获得了 94 分的评价，鲁尼的评论将其描述为“独特的影响力”。

paras.en: Looking to squeak into the top 10 is Burns & Co and Fathom Entertainment’s Jimmy, with the Jimmy Stewart biopic collecting $832,000 Friday from 1,470 North American theaters for a likely $2 million frame. Scheck’s review calls star KJ Apa “top-notch” but deems director Aaron Burns’ film “heartfelt to a fault.”
paras.zh: Burns & Co 和 Fathom Entertainment 的《吉米》有望跻身前十名，其吉米·斯图尔特传记片周五在北美 1,470 家影院上映，票房为 832,000 美元，预计票房为 200 万美元。谢克的评论称主演 KJ 阿帕“一流”，但认为导演亚伦·伯恩斯的电影“发自内心的过分”。

paras.en: Another Oscar hopeful launched in platform release as A24 debuted Club Kid on six screens, with the Cannes standout grossing $175,398 on Friday. Making his feature directorial debut, Jordan Firstman also stars as a party promoter who learns he has a 10-year-old son. Set to expand into Thanksgiving, it boasts a sterling 100 score from reviewers on Rotten Tomatoes, with THR critic Richard Lawson heralding it as “winning and clever.”
paras.zh: 另一位有望获得奥斯卡奖的影片《A24》在六块银幕上首次亮相，该片在戛纳电影节上周五获得了 175,398 美元的票房收入。乔丹·福斯特曼 (Jordan Firstman) 首次执导长片，他还饰演一名派对发起人，得知自己有一个 10 岁的儿子。该片将于感恩节上映，在烂番茄上获得了 100 分的高分，THR 评论家理查德·劳森 (Richard Lawson) 称赞它“成功且聪明”。

paras.en: Amazon MGM Studios releases I Play Rocky in seven locations, and it grossed around $160,000 on Friday. Anthony Ippolito stars as Sylvester Stallone in director Peter Farrelly’s making-of story for the 1976 classic Rocky. In his review, Rooney wrote that the movie — which holds an 88 Rotten Tomatoes score from critics — creates “a wave of warm nostalgia.”
paras.zh: 亚马逊米高梅影业公司在 7 个地点发行了《I Play Rocky》，该片周五的票房收入约为 16 万美元。安东尼·伊波利托在导演彼得·法拉利 1976 年经典电影《洛奇》的制作故事中饰演西尔维斯特·史泰龙。鲁尼在评论中写道，这部电影——烂番茄评分为 88 分——创造了“一股温暖的怀旧浪潮”。

paras.en: Among holdovers, A24’s much-discussed Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything looks to pull in around $8 million for the weekend as it competes with Ramayana and Drummer Boy for third place. The domestic cume for directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s feature stands at $73.4 million through Friday.
paras.zh: 在保留的影片中，A24 备受讨论的伊丽莎白·霍尔姆斯纪录片《你可以看到一切》周末有望获得约 800 万美元的票房，与《罗摩衍那》和《鼓手男孩》争夺第三名。截至周五，导演内森·菲尔德 (Nathan Fielder) 和兰斯·奥本海姆 (Lance Oppenheim) 的这部影片在国内的票房收入为 7,340 万美元。

paras.en: Next weekend brings the Johnny Depp studio comeback vehicle Ebenezer, along with How to Rob a Bank and Paper Tiger.
paras.zh: 下周末，约翰尼·德普工作室的《Ebenezer》将回归，另外还有《如何抢劫银行》和《纸老虎》。

articles.title: ‘Nobody Wants This’ Stars Hint at Season 4 and Declare Timothy Simons “the Lead of the Show Now”
articles.author: Kirsten Chuba

paras.en: On the same day that Nobody Wants This was renewed for a fourth season, the cast and crew came together to break down season three and tease what may be coming next.
paras.zh: 在《无人想要》续订第四季的同一天，演员和工作人员齐聚一堂，对第三季进行了分析，并预告了接下来可能发生的事情。

paras.en: Stars Kristen Bell, Justine Lupe, Timothy Simons and Jackie Tohn joined co-showrunner Bruce Eric Kaplan for the FYC conversation in L.A. on Friday, alongside costume designer Negar Ali-Kline and music supervisor Manish Raval. Noticeably absent was Adam Brody, as the crowd was told he is currently in production on a project in the U.K.; ahead of season three, Brody declared his support for a free Palestine, which creator Erin Foster and co-star Tovah Feldshuh have both publicly disagreed with. Foster and co-showrunner Jenni Konner were also not present at the event.
paras.zh: 周五，明星克里斯汀·贝尔、贾斯汀·卢佩、蒂莫西·西蒙斯和杰基·托恩与联合剧集制作人布鲁斯·埃里克·卡普兰一起参加了在洛杉矶举行的 FYC 对话，此外还有服装设计师内加尔·阿里·克莱恩和音乐总监曼尼什·拉瓦尔。值得注意的是亚当·布罗迪缺席了，因为观众被告知他目前正在英国拍摄一个项目；在第三季开始前，布罗迪宣布支持自由的巴勒斯坦，但主创艾琳·福斯特和联合主演托瓦·费尔德舒都公开表示反对。福斯特和联合剧集主管珍妮·康纳也没有出席活动。

paras.en: The conversation began with a mention of the season four renewal, as Bell told the room, “I know a couple things which are really exciting, but I’m just excited to read the drafts.” Simons added that after Bell and Brody’s characters had a surprise wedding to end season three, “I personally am really excited to see the families’ reaction to that because it was very romantic, them getting married like on a lark at the ocean.”
paras.zh: 谈话首先提到了第四季的续订，贝尔告诉房间里的人，“我知道一些非常令人兴奋的事情，但我只是很高兴阅读草稿。”西蒙斯补充说，在贝尔和布罗迪的角色在第三季结束时举行了一场惊喜婚礼后，“我个人很高兴看到家人对此的反应，因为这非常浪漫，他们就像在海边轻快地结婚一样。”

paras.en: Much of the chat, though, was dedicated to the episode where Simons’ character Sasha and Lupe’s character Morgan go to New York and finally act on their seasons-long chemistry. Simons said the pair was “very flattered and very excited” that they would get an episode just focusing on their characters, and “I do think that we approached it being like, for lack of a better term, ‘let’s not fuck this up.'”
paras.zh: 不过，大部分的聊天内容都是关于西蒙斯饰演的萨莎和卢佩饰演的摩根前往纽约并最终发挥出他们长达一季的化学反应的这一集。西蒙斯表示，两人“非常受宠若惊，非常兴奋”，因为他们能得到一集只专注于他们的角色的剧集，“我确实认为，我们的处理方式就像，因为没有更好的术语，‘我们不要搞砸了。’”

paras.en: “It was a lane that I don’t think either of us had ever really played in before,” the actor continued. “We got to be two sort of oddballs doing a romantic comedy; I didn’t have to be super smoky-eyed, I got to be a little bit of a funhouse-mirror version of a romantic lead.”
paras.zh: “我认为我们以前都没有真正在这条巷子里玩过，”这位演员继续说道。 “我们必须是两个奇怪的人来演一部浪漫喜剧；我不必是超级烟熏眼，我必须是一个浪漫主角的滑稽镜子版本。”

paras.en: Simons joked that with both he and Lupe being quite tall, “so much of us is limb and there are so many elbows,” causing them to be quite nervous about how to pull off a rom-com-worthy kiss. Lupe teased, “Bruce, like we literally came up to you and were like, ‘You have to make us not look bad during this kiss. Choreograph the shit out of it; it has to be something like kind of cute.'”
paras.zh: 西蒙斯开玩笑说，由于他和卢佩都很高，“我们很多人都是肢体，而且有很多肘部”，这让他们对如何完成浪漫喜剧般的吻感到非常紧张。卢佩调侃道，“布鲁斯，就像我们真的走到你面前说的那样，‘你必须让我们在这个吻中看起来不那么糟糕。精心编排它；它必须是有点可爱的东西。’”

paras.en: It seems to have worked out, with the episode being a breakout moment from season three. Bell gave her full endorsement, saying, “The whole New York episode I think is one of the best episodes of television that has ever been made. I was standing up watching the cut” and “my body was aching for them to be together.”
paras.zh: 这似乎已经成功了，这一集是第三季的突破时刻。贝尔给予了她充分的认可，她说：“我认为整个纽约剧集是有史以来最好的电视剧集之一。我站着看剪辑”并且“我的身体渴望他们在一起。”

paras.en: Lupe interjected, “She was also live texting me and Tim about how hot Tim was.” Bell confirmed, “I was like, ‘You guys, Tim is a romantic lead.’ I said it, everyone’s gonna know it. We’re gonna need security on set next year. He’s the lead of the show now — somebody’s gotta tell Adam.”
paras.zh: 卢佩插话道：“她还实时给我和蒂姆发短信，告诉我蒂姆有多性感。”贝尔证实，“我当时想，‘你们这些家伙，蒂姆是个浪漫的主角。’我说了，每个人都会知道。明年我们需要在片场保安。他现在是这部剧的主角——必须得有人告诉亚当。”

paras.en: Nobody Wants This is currently streaming on Netflix.
paras.zh: 《无人想要》目前正在 Netflix 上播放。

articles.title: Connor Wood Reveals What Happened on 8th Avenue With Jennifer Lawrence in New Smoothie King Collab: “Missed My Moment” (Exclusive)
articles.author: McKinley Franklin

paras.en: Connor Wood is coming clean about what really led to Jennifer Lawrence‘s viral comment about seeing him on 8th avenue and him paying her no mind.
paras.zh: 康纳·伍德 (Connor Wood) 坦白了詹妮弗·劳伦斯 (Jennifer Lawrence) 在第八大道见到他，而他却对她毫不在意的言论走红的真正原因。

paras.en: The Dancing With the Stars season 35 contestant teamed up with Smoothie King to debut “Connor’s Paid Me No Mind Smoothie,” which launched Thursday, a play on the trendy moment sparked by the Oscar winner.
paras.zh: 这位《与星共舞》第 35 季的参赛者与 Smoothie King 合作推出了首部作品《Connor's Paid Me No Mind Smoothie》，该剧于周四推出，这是一部由奥斯卡奖得主引发的时尚时刻。

paras.en: Wood and Lawrence’s meta exchange occurred after he admitted she was his celebrity crush in an interview with BuzzFeed Celeb, and she commented, “I saw you on 8th avenue drinking a smoothie and you paid me no mind.” The Hunger Games star’s remark stunned the comedian, leading to a number of memes and a wave of virality, so much so that Wood collaborated with Smoothie King.
paras.zh: 伍德和劳伦斯的元交流发生在劳伦斯在接受 BuzzFeed Celeb 采访时承认她是他迷恋的名人之后，劳伦斯评论道：“我看到你在第八大道喝冰沙，但你没有理会我。”这位《饥饿游戏》明星的言论震惊了这位喜剧演员，引发了一系列表情包和病毒式传播，以至于伍德与 Smoothie King 合作。

paras.en: “I think enough time has passed that I can break my silence about what happened on 8th avenue that day,” Wood said in a new video (watch below). “I was preoccupied that day. I was distracted. I missed my moment. I dropped the ball.”
paras.zh: “我认为已经过去了足够的时间，我可以打破对那天在第八大道发生的事情的沉默，”伍德在一段新视频中说道（见下文）。 “那天我全神贯注。我心烦意乱。我错过了最佳时机。我把球丢了。”

paras.en: “Not this time, OK, this time, I’m paying mind. I’m a changed man. I’ll never not pay attention again. My eyes are up. My mind is open. My body is nourished, right,” he said while holding his smoothie. Additional shots of Wood looking alert, walking around outside were shown, as a pedestrian even told him, “Oh hey, I saw you on 8th ave!”
paras.zh: “这一次，好吧，这一次，我注意了。我变了一个人。我再也不会不注意了。我的眼睛向上。我的思想开放。我的身体得到了滋养，对吧，”他一边说，一边拿着冰沙。伍德在外面走来走去，神情警惕，一名行人甚至告诉他，“哦嘿，我在第八大道看到你了！”的其他镜头。

paras.en: “Connor’s Paid Me No Mind” smoothie features 26g of protein and 0g of added sugar per 20 oz. cup, made with whole strawberries and bananas plus electrolytes to support hydration.
paras.zh: “Connor's Paid Me No Mind”冰沙每 20 盎司含有 26 克蛋白质和 0 克添加糖。杯子，由整个草莓和香蕉加上电解质制成，以支持水分。

articles.title: Why the prognosis for healthcare stocks is uncertain ahead of Congress’ new makeup

paras.en: Healthcare stocks may struggle to gain momentum as Democrats prepare to take over Congress.
paras.zh: 随着民主党准备接管国会，医疗保健股可能难以获得动力。

paras.en: Jared Holz, who covers healthcare for Mizuho, says the outlook for the sector is uncertain because of likely gridlock between lawmakers.
paras.zh: 负责瑞穗医疗保健业务的贾里德·霍尔兹 (Jared Holz) 表示，由于立法者之间可能出现僵局，该行业的前景不确定。

paras.en: "The next couple of years I really can't see too much happening," the firm's sector specialist told CNBC's "Fast Money" on Wednesday. "I'm not sure you want to own everything, but you can pick and choose the names… Pharma is trading more expensive than tech for the first time in 20 years. So, I backed away from pharma. I would look at medtech."
paras.zh: 该公司的行业专家周三对 CNBC 的“快钱”节目表示：“我真的看不到未来几年会发生太多事情。” “我不确定你想拥有一切，但你可以选择名称……制药公司的交易价格 20 年来首次超过科技公司。所以，我放弃了制药公司。我会关注医疗科技公司。”

paras.en: The State Street Health Care Select ETF (XLV) jumped 3% a day after Election Day.
paras.zh: 选举日后，道富医疗精选 ETF (XLV) 每天上涨 3%。

paras.en: "You had this very weird situation where typically you wouldn't have all of these categories work in tandem, and they did. So, I think some things just a little bit off," said Holz, a day before healthcare got swept up in Thursday's Wall Street sell-off.
paras.zh: “你遇到了一种非常奇怪的情况，通常情况下你不会让所有这些类别同时发挥作用，但他们做到了。所以，我认为有些事情有点不对劲，”霍尔茨在周四的华尔街抛售中医疗保健被席卷的前一天说道。

paras.en: According to Holz, healthcare's real booster shot may come if a Democrat wins the White House in 2028.
paras.zh: Holz 表示，如果民主党在 2028 年入主白宫，医疗保健行业真正的强心针可能就会到来。

paras.en: "Then I think you see some of the Trump strategies rolled back. That's where I think healthcare could actually perform well," said Holz, who added it hinges on Democrats retaining the Senate and House.
paras.zh: 霍尔茨说：“然后我认为你会看到特朗普的一些战略被撤销。这就是我认为医疗保健实际上可以表现良好的地方。”他补充说，这取决于民主党能否保住参议院和众议院。

paras.en: For investors who are long on healthcare, Holz said each subsector should be treated differently.
paras.zh: 霍尔兹表示，对于看好医疗保健的投资者来说，每个子行业都应该受到不同的对待。

paras.en: "Can we get some of the regulation that has taken place over the past couple of years and overturn that over the near term? I don't necessarily believe so," Holz said. "But if you do, then you probably want to be long some of these medical device stocks that are at or near multi-year lows."
paras.zh: “我们能否获得过去几年实施的一些监管并在短期内推翻它？我不一定这么认为，”霍尔茨说。 “但如果你这样做，那么你可能想做多一些处于或接近多年低点的医疗器械股票。”

paras.en: The State Street Health Care Select ETF ended virtually flat this week. It's up around 32% since President Trump took office in January 2025 — beating the S&P 500 by almost 9 percentage points.
paras.zh: 道富医疗精选 ETF 本周收盘基本持平。自特朗普总统 2025 年 1 月上任以来，该指数上涨了约 32%，高出标准普尔 500 指数近 9 个百分点。

articles.title: Expanding on naval blockade, U.S. military looks to restrict Iranian land commerce

paras.en: Building on a months-long naval blockade on Iran, the U.S. military said on Saturday it is launching a task force to help crack down on Tehran's movement of advanced weapons and other sanctioned material over its land borders and through the Caspian Sea.
paras.zh: 在对伊朗长达数月的海上封锁的基础上，美国军方周六表示，将组建一支特遣部队，帮助打击德黑兰通过其陆地边界和里海运送先进武器和其他受制裁物资的行为。

paras.en: Task Force Iron Gate, which was first reported by Reuters, will be based in Tampa, Florida, and will coordinate with other U.S. government agencies. Beyond the movement of weapons, it will also focus on halting the flow of dual-use technologies used by Iran and stemming what Washington calls illegal revenue streams.
paras.zh: 路透社首先报道了“铁门”特遣部队，该部队将驻扎在佛罗里达州坦帕市，并将与其他美国政府机构进行协调。除了武器流动之外，它还将重点阻止伊朗使用的军民两用技术的流动，并阻止华盛顿所谓的非法收入来源。

paras.en: The establishment of the task force is the latest illustration of how the U.S. is still searching for ways to increase pressure on Tehran, more than eight months after launching with Israel a war against the Islamic Republic.
paras.zh: 该特别工作组的成立是美国在与以色列发动针对伊朗伊斯兰共和国的战争八个多月后仍在寻找加大对德黑兰压力的最新例证。

paras.en: While U.S. strikes have dealt devastating blows to Iran's conventional military and the U.S. naval blockade has severely restricted its crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz and the Arabian Sea, Iran still poses a formidable threat to the region, and its rulers have tightened their grip on the country.
paras.zh: 尽管美国的打击对伊朗常规军事造成毁灭性打击，美国海上封锁严重限制了伊朗通过霍尔木兹海峡和阿拉伯海的原油出口，但伊朗仍然对该地区构成巨大威胁，其统治者加强了对该国的控制。

paras.en: A Reuters investigation found Iran has created a secret network of military agencies to import at least $2 billion in hardware, explosives and heavy-duty trucks since January 2025, evading both the US naval blockade and Western sanctions.
paras.zh: 路透社的一项调查发现，伊朗建立了一个军事机构秘密网络，自 2025 年 1 月以来进口了至少 20 亿美元的硬件、炸药和重型卡车，逃避美国海军封锁和西方制裁。

paras.en: The material entered Iran by cargo ship across the Caspian Sea from Russia, by truck from Central Asia, and by freight planes from China, the Reuters investigation showed.
paras.zh: 路透社的调查显示，这些材料通过货船从俄罗斯跨越里海进入伊朗，通过卡车从中亚进入伊朗，并通过货机从中国进入伊朗。

paras.en: U.S. Central Command said the task force will coordinate with other government agencies. A U.S. military official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said that was expected to include the Treasury, State, and Justice Departments, as well as the intelligence community.
paras.zh: 美国中央司令部表示，特别工作组将与其他政府机构进行协调。一位不愿透露姓名的美国军方官员表示，预计将包括财政部、国务院、司法部以及情报部门。

paras.en: "Strengthening CENTCOM's collaboration with US interagency partners will further constrain Iran's ability to finance terrorism, rebuild weapons factories, and replenish their military," Admiral Brad Cooper, the commander of Central Command, said in a statement.
paras.zh: 中央司令部司令布拉德·库珀上将在一份声明中表示：“加强中央司令部与美国跨部门合作伙伴的合作将进一步限制伊朗资助恐怖主义、重建武器工厂和补充军队的能力。”

paras.en: Central Command estimated that its naval blockade has prevented Iran from exporting more than $25 billion in crude oil.
paras.zh: 中央司令部估计，其海上封锁已阻止伊朗出口超过 250 亿美元的原油。

paras.en: Still, Iran has proven resilient and gloated after U.S. midterm election results that punished U.S. President Donald Trump's Republican Party, giving control of Congress to opposition Democrats. Vice President JD Vance blamed the Iran war for the electoral rout and appeared to question whether the conflict was worth it.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，在美国中期选举结果惩罚了美国总统唐纳德·特朗普的共和党，将国会控制权让给反对派民主党后，伊朗表现出了坚韧和幸灾乐祸的态度。副总统万斯将选举溃败归咎于伊朗战争，并似乎质疑这场冲突是否值得。

paras.en: Mediators have intensified efforts in recent days to end the war between Iran and the U.S. amid fears it could reignite after the U.S. midterm elections.
paras.zh: 由于担心美国中期选举后战争可能重新燃起，调停者最近几天加紧努力结束伊朗和美国之间的战争。

paras.en: Trump has been threatened with carrying out a new offensive against Iran, putting countries in the Gulf on edge, since Tehran has threatened broad retaliation against Gulf infrastructure.
paras.zh: 特朗普受到威胁要对伊朗发动新的攻势，这让海湾国家处于紧张状态，因为德黑兰威胁要对海湾基础设施进行广泛报复。

paras.en: Reuters has reported that U.S. intelligence assessments in recent months have indicated that renewed strikes on Iran would not fundamentally change Tehran's negotiating position or lead to the fall of Iran's government.
paras.zh: 路透社报道称，美国近几个月的情报评估表明，对伊朗的新一轮打击不会从根本上改变德黑兰的谈判立场，也不会导致伊朗政府垮台。

articles.title: Meta chief strategy officer Dave Wehner leaves to join AI infrastructure startup Fireworks as CFO

paras.en: Dave Wehner, Meta's chief strategy officer, is leaving the company for four-year-old AI startup Fireworks.
paras.zh: Meta 首席战略官 Dave Wehner 将离开公司，前往成立四年的人工智能初创公司 Fireworks。

paras.en: At Fireworks — an AI inference and model-training platform focused on open models that was valued at $17.5 billion during a Series D fundraising round in July — Wehner will assume the CFO role, he announced on X on Friday.
paras.zh: Fireworks 是一个专注于开放模型的人工智能推理和模型训练平台，在 7 月份的 D 轮融资中估值为 175 亿美元。Wehner 在周五的 X 上宣布，他将担任首席财务官一职。

paras.en: Wehner will be tasked with scaling the company's finances and operations, Fireworks CEO Lin Qiao said in a statement to CNBC.
paras.zh: Fireworks 首席执行官林乔在给 CNBC 的一份声明中表示，Wehner 将负责扩大公司的财务和运营规模。

paras.en: "Fireworks has the right mission for the moment," Wehner wrote on X, adding: "I've become increasingly bullish on what they are building. There's a remarkable depth of technical talent here, coupled with a very practical focus on what customers need."
paras.zh: “Fireworks 目前拥有正确的使命，”Wehner 在 X 上写道，并补充道：“我越来越看好他们正​​在开发的产品。这里拥有深厚的技术人才，而且非常注重客户需求。”

paras.en: The AI startup, founded in 2022 by former Meta and Google employees, is a platform that lets developers customize and run open models for their businesses. Its latest investment round was led by Atreides Management, Index Ventures and TCV, but Fireworks is also backed by Nvidia and Sequoia Capital. Business Insider reported that it is in early talks to raise funds again at a possible $30 billion to $40 billion valuation.
paras.zh: 这家人工智能初创公司由 Meta 和 Google 前员工于 2022 年创立，是一个让开发人员为其业务定制和运行开放模型的平台。 Fireworks 最新一轮投资由 Atreides Management、Index Ventures 和 TCV 领投，但 Fireworks 也得到了 Nvidia 和红杉资本的支持。据 Business Insider 报道，该公司正在就再次融资进行早期谈判，估值可能为 300 亿至 400 亿美元。

paras.en: Wehner joined Meta, then called Facebook, in 2012 and was the company's chief financial officer from 2014 to 2022.
paras.zh: 韦纳于 2012 年加入 Meta（当时称为 Facebook），并于 2014 年至 2022 年担任该公司的首席财务官。

paras.en: "Dave helped guide Meta through tremendous growth and complexity over 14 years, and brought disciplined thinking to some of our hardest company-level decisions," Meta COO Javier Olivan said in a statement to CNBC.
paras.zh: Meta 首席运营官哈维尔·奥利文 (Javier Olivan) 在向 CNBC 发表的一份声明中表示：“Dave 帮助引导 Meta 度过了 14 年来的巨大增长和复杂性，并为我们公司层面的一些最艰难的决策带来了严谨的思维。”

paras.en: Fireworks is notably smaller than Meta — the tech giant has about a $1.56 trillion market capitalization as of Friday's close — and its competitors, which include OpenAI and Anthropic.
paras.zh: Fireworks 的规模明显小于 Meta（截至周五收盘，这家科技巨头的市值约为 1.56 万亿美元）及其竞争对手，其中包括 OpenAI 和 Anthropic。

paras.en: "Dave told me he wanted to get back to a smaller company where he could build toward a big impact again," Fireworks' Lin wrote in a LinkedIn post on Friday. "He sees AI as the defining technology shift of his lifetime and wants to help shape what comes next."
paras.zh: “戴夫告诉我，他想回到一家较小的公司，在那里他可以再次产生巨大的影响，”Fireworks 的林周五在 LinkedIn 帖子中写道。 “他将人工智能视为他一生中决定性的技术转变，并希望帮助塑造接下来的发展。”

paras.en: The company's size has not made it immune to the risks and complications often associated with AI technology. In October, the company found "a security incident involving unauthorized use of internal Fireworks credentials," in which "an unauthorized third party accessed environment variables used in evaluation jobs in a limited number of customer accounts," it said in a press release.
paras.zh: 该公司的规模并不能使其免受通常与人工智能技术相关的风险和并发症的影响。该公司在一份新闻稿中表示，10 月份，该公司发现了“一起涉及未经授权使用内部 Fireworks 凭据的安全事件”，其中“未经授权的第三方访问了有限数量的客户帐户中评估作业中使用的环境变量”。

paras.en: "Based on our investigation at this time, we have not detected evidence of unauthorized access to customer models, datasets, training data, personal information, or inference traffic within the Fireworks security perimeter or control," the release said.
paras.zh: 新闻稿称：“根据我们目前的调查，我们尚未发现未经授权访问 Fireworks 安全范围或控制范围内的客户模型、数据集、训练数据、个人信息或推理流量的证据。”

articles.title: Nothing can be fully transparent, physicists discover

paras.en: The Guinness Book of World Records lists Ivan Smalyukh as the inventor of the most transparent material known. His lab at the University of Colorado Boulder has developed gels that could be used for window insulation by carefully tuning them until they bent light almost as little as air does, making them clearer than the glass itself.
paras.zh: 吉尼斯世界纪录将 Ivan Smalyukh 列为已知最透明材料的发明者。他在科罗拉多大学博尔德分校的实验室开发了可用于窗户隔热的凝胶，通过仔细调整凝胶，直到它们对光线的弯曲几乎与空气一样小，使它们比玻璃本身更透明。

paras.en: His work and other recent advances might suggest that researchers are on a path toward developing a completely transparent substance. That dream was recently proved false, however, when a group of theoretical physicists found that no light-bending material can ever be fully transparent, owing to a quantum process that turns waves of light into waves of sound. The researchers argue that even the cleverest engineering will never be able to create a material that doesn’t lose some of the light that passes through it. But the loss can be very, very small.
paras.zh: 他的工作和其他最新进展可能表明研究人员正在开发一种完全透明的物质。然而，这个梦想最近被证明是错误的，一群理论物理学家发现，由于将光波转变为声波的量子过程，任何光弯曲材料都不可能是完全透明的。研究人员认为，即使是最聪明的工程也永远无法创造出一种不会损失一些穿过它的光线的材料。但损失可能非常非常小。

paras.en: Smalyukh’s gels already get pretty close. But they’re designed to be applied thinly: a foot-thick layer would transmit very little light.
paras.zh: Smalyukh 的凝胶已经非常接近了。但它们的设计目的是薄涂：一英尺厚的层只能透过很少的光。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: If you want to see farther, you’d have better luck peering through a fiber-optic cable, like those used to link the Internet across the ocean. Fiber optics carry light on bending paths for miles before they need to amplify signals for the next section of cable.
paras.zh: 如果你想看得更远，你最好通过光纤电缆来观察，就像那些用于跨洋连接互联网的电缆一样。光纤在弯曲路径上传输光线数英里，然后需要为下一段电缆放大信号。

paras.en: To do even better, you might turn to a stranger substance. Cool helium down to only a few degrees above absolute zero, and it becomes a kind of liquid known as a superfluid. In a superfluid, quantum mechanics coordinates the way different atoms move, letting the liquid flow with no friction at all. Liquid helium, in particular, is astonishingly clear, and although it absorbs x-rays, scientists have not been able to measure an effect on visible light.
paras.zh: 为了做得更好，你可能会转向一种陌生的物质。将氦冷却到仅比绝对零高几度，它就变成一种被称为超流体的液体。在超流体中，量子力学协调不同原子的运动方式，让液体毫无摩擦地流动。尤其是液氦，其透明度惊人，虽然它能吸收 X 射线，但科学家们还无法测量对可见光的影响。

paras.en: Theoretical physicists Alberto Nicolis, Federico Piazza and Angelo Esposito have spent their careers thinking about strange quantum materials such as superfluid helium. Nicolis and Piazza were curious about what would happen to a material that was as transparent as possible. It would have to be cold, so that light didn’t get lost in the jiggling of already moving molecules, and inert, with no chemical reactions or electric currents that might absorb light as a source of energy. They expected that such a material would still absorb some light particles, called photons, through subtle quantum processes, and they set out to estimate how much light would be lost.
paras.zh: 理论物理学家阿尔贝托·尼科利斯 (Alberto Nicolis)、费德里科·皮亚扎 (Federico Piazza) 和安杰洛·埃斯波西托 (Angelo Esposito) 的职业生涯一直在思考超流氦等奇怪的量子材料。尼科利斯和皮亚扎很好奇，尽可能透明的材料会发生什么。它必须是冷的，这样光就不会在已经移动的分子的抖动中丢失，并且必须是惰性的，没有化学反应或电流可能吸收光作为能量来源。他们预计这种材料仍然会通过微妙的量子过程吸收一些称为光子的光粒子，并且他们开始估计会损失多少光。

paras.en: Nicolis and Piazza told this to Esposito, who realized he had made a similar estimate—not for light but for dark matter. He had been trying to figure out how to detect a hypothetical particle called a dark photon and realized it could potentially be found if it nudged an atomic nucleus in superfluid helium.
paras.zh: 尼科利斯和皮亚扎将此事告诉了埃斯波西托，埃斯波西托意识到自己也做出了类似的估计——不是针对光物质，而是针对暗物质。他一直试图弄清楚如何检测一种称为暗光子的假想粒子，并意识到如果它推动超流氦中的原子核，就有可能发现它。

paras.en: “In interacting with one of the nuclei, it gives it a kick,” Esposito says.
paras.zh: “在与其中一个原子核相互作用时，它会给它带来冲击，”埃斯波西托说。

paras.en: That kick would trigger a tiny vibration, a kind of quantum mechanical sound wave. As this happens again and again, the dark photons would lose energy. Esposito realized the same thing should happen to normal photons. Eventually the photons would lose so much energy that they would be undetectable.
paras.zh: 那一脚会引发微小的振动，一种量子力学声波。当这种情况一次又一次发生时，暗光子就会失去能量。埃斯波西托意识到同样的事情也应该发生在普通光子上。最终，光子会损失大量能量，以至于无法被检测到。

paras.en: That “eventually” can be a long time. The perfect superfluid the physicists imagined is so clear that light could travel across the diameter of Earth before it becomes noticeably fainter. But eventually the light would still fade. And while the researchers’ model only describes superfluids, they expect other materials to follow similar rules.
paras.zh: 这个“最终”可能会很长一段时间。物理学家想象的完美超流体是如此清晰，以至于光可以在变得明显变暗之前穿过地球的直径。但最终，光芒还是会消退。虽然研究人员的模型仅描述了超流体，但他们预计其他材料也遵循类似的规则。

paras.en: “I think it’s universal for all materials,” Esposito says. The group posted its findings as a preprint on the website arXiv.org on October 8.
paras.zh: “我认为它对所有材料都是通用的，”埃斯波西托说。该小组于 10 月 8 日将其研究结果作为预印本发布在 arXiv.org 网站上。

paras.en: “I find this work super interesting,” says Borna Salehian, a physicist at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Zurich, who was not involved with the project. “In theoretical physics, we look for fundamental limitations set by nature. This paper precisely gives one!”
paras.zh: “我发现这项工作非常有趣，”瑞士苏黎世联邦理工学院的物理学家博尔纳·萨利安（Borna Salehian）说道，他没有参与该项目。 “在理论物理学中，我们寻找大自然设定的基本限制。这篇论文恰恰给出了一个！”

articles.title: The mathematical trick that explains how to find a needle in a haystack

paras.en: Finding a needle in a haystack is a metaphor for a task that is nigh impossible. But here at Scientific American, we wanted to know: Exactly how hard is it, really, to find a needle in a haystack?
paras.zh: 大海捞针比喻几乎不可能完成的任务。但在《科学美国人》，我们想知道：大海捞针究竟有多难？

paras.en: The short answer is: very, very hard, says Jeffrey Rosenthal, a statistics professor at the University of Toronto. While published literature on the math of literally looking for needles in actual stacks of hay are thin on the ground, the principles of such a search lie in an area of math called probabilities.
paras.zh: 多伦多大学统计学教授杰弗里·罗森塔尔（Jeffrey Rosenthal）表示，简短的回答是：非常非常难。虽然关于在实际干草堆中寻找针的数学文献很少，但这种搜索的原理在于一个称为概率的数学领域。

paras.en: “Probability theory as a field is the mathematical study of randomness and uncertainty, and that has everything from very mathematical theorems, and so on, to very applied things about the real world,” Rosenthal says.
paras.zh: 罗森塔尔说：“概率论作为一个领域，是对随机性和不确定性的数学研究，它涵盖了从非常数学定理等到现实世界中非常实用的事物的一切内容。”

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: To apply those principles to the haystack challenge, the first step is to figure out the numbers behind the problem. Let’s assume the haystack is approximately three feet wide, three feet long and eight feet high, or about 125,000 cubic inches in size (for reference, the interior of a Honda Civic is around 171,000 cubic inches).
paras.zh: 要将这些原则应用于大海捞针挑战，第一步是找出问题背后的数字。我们假设干草堆大约有 3 英尺宽、3 英尺长和 8 英尺高，即尺寸约为 125,000 立方英寸（作为参考，本田思域的内部空间约为 171,000 立方英寸）。

paras.en: Like any problem, Rosenthal says, the best way to start is by breaking it down into smaller, manageable chunks—in this case, quite literally.
paras.zh: 罗森塔尔说，就像任何问题一样，最好的开始方法是将其分解为更小的、可管理的块——在这种情况下，毫不夸张地说。

paras.en: “I thought, ‘Maybe you take one cubic inch at a time,’ as a rough-eyed way to think about it,” he says. In other words, you would have 125,000 separate cubic inches, and you’d have to look through each one at a time.
paras.zh: “我想，‘也许你一次只取一立方英寸’，这是一种粗略的思考方式，”他说。换句话说，您将拥有 125,000 立方英寸的独立空间，并且您必须一次查看每一个。

paras.en: Rosenthal estimates that you could look through one cubic inch per second. That works out to about 35 hours straight of looking through small clumps of hay for a needle. Fortunately, each individual clump has a one-in-125,000 chance of containing said needle. And who knows, you might find it in the very first clump. Or you could be sifting through tiny bundles of hay for almost a day and a half.
paras.zh: 罗森塔尔估计，你每秒可以看透一立方英寸。这相当于连续 35 个小时在小块干草中寻找针头。幸运的是，每个单独的团块都有 125,000 分之一的机会包含所述针。谁知道呢，你可能会在第一丛中找到它。或者您可能会花近一天半的时间筛选小捆干草。

paras.en: Given that most people need time to eat, sleep, and generally do other things than fiddle with dried pieces of grass, Rosenthal says, you could limit your search to eight hours.
paras.zh: 罗森塔尔说，考虑到大多数人需要时间吃饭、睡觉和做其他事情，而不是摆弄干草，你可以将搜索时间限制在八个小时内。

paras.en: “Eight out of that almost 35 hours works out to about a 23 percent” chance of finding the needle per day, he says.
paras.zh: 他说，“在这近 35 个小时中，每天有 8 个小时找到针头的几率约为 23%”。

paras.en: You might be able to use another, more geometric approach in which you convert the three-dimensional stack of hay into a flat mat, but Rosenthal says that may present new challenges.
paras.zh: 您也许可以使用另一种更具几何形状的方法，将三维干草堆转换成平坦的垫子，但罗森塔尔表示，这可能会带来新的挑战。

paras.en: “The flatter you make it, the more easy it might be to find a needle within a little piece,” he says. “But also, it will be bigger and wider when you flatten it out.”
paras.zh: “你做得越平，就越容易在一小块内找到一根针，”他说。 “而且，当你把它压平时，它会变得更大更宽。”

paras.en: There is a way to cheat: needle-in-a-haystack-like problems have become an interesting challenge for machine-learning designers, whereby artificial intelligence models must be trained to detect the difference between a needle and its surroundings. But like most humans, the majority of these efforts use “find a needle in a haystack” as an analogy for another task rather than literally performing that search.
paras.zh: 有一种作弊的方法：大海捞针般的问题已经成为机器学习设计者面临的一个有趣的挑战，必须训练人工智能模型来检测针与其周围环境之间的差异。但与大多数人一样，这些努力中的大多数都使用“大海捞针”作为另一项任务的类比，而不是字面上执行该搜索。

paras.en: Rosenthal points out that while AI models have helped solve some of the most puzzling math problems of our time, they haven’t been used much for probabilities—yet.
paras.zh: 罗森塔尔指出，虽然人工智能模型帮助解决了我们这个时代一些最令人费解的数学问题，但它们还没有被广泛用于概率研究。

paras.en: “Maybe they won’t notice us for a little while,” he says, referring to his field. “But I’m sure it’s coming.”
paras.zh: “也许他们暂时不会注意到我们，”他指的是他的领域。 “但我确信它会到来。”

articles.title: Earth's rocks have a missing layer spanning up to a billion years. Scientists finally know what happened to it

paras.en: Imagine opening a history book and finding several chapters torn out. This was what geologists looking into the rock records of Earth’s past discovered on several continents in the 1870s.
paras.zh: 想象一下打开一本历史书，发现有几章被撕掉了。这是 1870 年代地质学家在研究地球过去的岩石记录时在几个大陆上发现的结果。

paras.en: They dubbed it the Great Unconformity. Where layers of rock often stack up in a steady sequence from oldest to youngest, in many places around the world there is a gap of hundreds of millions of years.
paras.zh: 他们称之为“大不整合”。岩层通常从最古老到最年轻的顺序稳定地堆积起来，在世界上许多地方，岩石层之间存在数亿年的差距。

paras.en: For 150 years, nobody has known what erased those missing chapters. In new research published in Nature, we finally provide an explanation: deep processes inside Earth lifted some continents high above the sea, where their surfaces were scoured down by the grinding movement of enormous sheets of ice.
paras.zh: 150 年来，没有人知道是什么抹去了那些缺失的章节。在《自然》杂志上发表的新研究中，我们最终提供了一个解释：地球内部的深层过程将一些大陆抬高到海平面以上，它们的表面被巨大冰层的研磨运动冲刷下来。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Layers of rock often stack up in chronological order, with the oldest at the bottom and the youngest at the top.
paras.zh: 岩石层通常按时间顺序堆叠起来，最古老的位于底部，最年轻的位于顶部。

paras.en: Yet in some places, such as the Grand Canyon in North America, you can touch rock layers from two different ages, hundreds of millions of years apart. A flat layer of sedimentary rock, about 540 million years old or younger, rests directly atop a crystalline “basement” up to two billion years old.
paras.zh: 然而在某些地方，例如北美的大峡谷，您可以触摸到两个不同时代、相隔数亿年的岩层。一层平坦的沉积岩，大约有 5.4 亿年或更早的历史，直接位于长达 20 亿年历史的结晶“基底”之上。

paras.en: Somewhere in between, a considerable chunk (up to a quarter) of Earth’s history has simply vanished.
paras.zh: 在这两者之间的某个地方，地球历史的很大一部分（最多四分之一）就这样消失了。

paras.en: Important things happened in that time. The sedimentary layers on the younger side of the Great Unconformity appear at the same time as a huge diversification in the forms of life on Earth. This is the so-called Cambrian explosion, which began around 540 million years ago.
paras.zh: 那时发生了重要的事情。大不整合面较新一侧的沉积层与地球上生命形式的巨大多样化同时出现。这就是所谓的寒武纪大爆发，大约开始于5.4亿年前。

paras.en: Scientists have speculated entire continents were eroded during the Great Unconformity, which may have altered the chemical balance of seawater and allowed animal life to flourish.
paras.zh: 科学家推测，在大不整合期间，整个大陆都受到了侵蚀，这可能改变了海水的化学平衡，使动物得以繁衍生息。

paras.en: Geologists have found evidence of the Great Unconformity throughout North America and parts of northern China, as well as beneath younger rocks in northern Europe. Yet its origin has remained a puzzle.
paras.zh: 地质学家在整个北美和中国北部部分地区以及北欧较年轻的岩石下发现了大不整合面的证据。然而它的起源仍然是一个谜。

paras.en: Some scientists have argued it was caused by erosion by massive ice sheets during the Snowball Earth period between 720 million years and 635 million years ago. Others have pointed to the reshuffling of continental blocks, mountain-building processes, heat-induced movement inside the Earth, volcanic activity, or global sea level change.
paras.zh: 一些科学家认为，这是由7.2亿年前到6.35亿年前的雪球地球时期大量冰盖的侵蚀造成的。其他人则指出了大陆块的重新洗牌、造山过程、地球内部热引起的运动、火山活动或全球海平面变化。

paras.en: Testing these hypotheses has been a challenge because the primary evidence consists of missing rock. As a result, we need to work from what we already know to fill in the gaps.
paras.zh: 测试这些假设一直是一个挑战，因为主要证据包括缺失的岩石。因此，我们需要根据已知的知识来填补空白。

paras.en: We had a theory that the creation of the Great Unconformity might have been influenced by heat-driven motion in Earth’s mantle. The mantle is a 2,900-kilometer thick layer of hot solid rock that slowly moves over tens to hundreds of millions of years. Hot mantle rises from deep beneath and cold mantle sinks, pushing and pulling the surface above.
paras.zh: 我们有一个理论，认为大不整合面的形成可能受到地幔热驱动运动的影响。地幔是一层 2,900 公里厚的炽热固体岩石层，在数千万至数亿年的时间里缓慢移动。热地幔从地下深处升起，冷地幔下沉，推动和拉动上方的地表。

paras.en: This huge, slow movement can raise or lower the surface by hundreds of meters. Continents sit on top of the mantle and get pushed up and down by its motion.
paras.zh: 这种巨大而缓慢的运动可以使地表升高或降低数百米。大陆位于地幔顶部，并被地幔的运动上下推动。

paras.en: We used the Australian supercomputer Gadi to model how the movement of the mantle had affected continents over the past billion years.
paras.zh: 我们使用澳大利亚超级计算机 Gadi 来模拟过去十亿年来地幔运动如何影响大陆。

paras.en: Our results consistently showed that mantle convection caused ancient continental blocks Laurentia (which now makes up much of North America), Baltica (parts of northern Europe), and North China to be lifted up from around a billion years ago to 540 million years ago. Over the past 540 million years, they have been pulled downward.
paras.zh: 我们的研究结果一致表明，地幔对流导致古代大陆块劳伦西亚（现在构成北美的大部分地区）、波罗的海（北欧的部分地区）和华北从大约 10 亿年前抬升到 5.4 亿年前。在过去的5.4亿年里，它们一直被向下拉。

paras.en: This up-and-down movement is the ideal scenario for the formation and preservation of the Great Unconformity. When these continental blocks were lifted up, we see the crystalline underlayer was at the surface – and the layers of sediment above were eroded away. Then when the blocks sank, new layers of sediment began to form, which are preserved in rock to this day.
paras.zh: 这种上下运动是大不整合面形成和保存的理想情景。当这些大陆块被抬起时，我们看到结晶底层位于地表，而上面的沉积物层被侵蚀掉了。然后，当这些块体下沉时，新的沉积物层开始形成，这些沉积物至今仍保存在岩石中。

paras.en: Importantly, the uplift predicted by our models coincided with the Snowball Earth period. During this period, enormous ice sheets scraped over the surface of continents for tens of millions of years.
paras.zh: 重要的是，我们的模型预测的隆起恰逢雪球地球时期。在此期间，巨大的冰盖在大陆表面刮擦了数千万年。

paras.en: Glaciers and ice sheets are more efficient than rivers at eroding continents, even on gentle slopes. The ice sheets would have slowly slid downhill across the uplifted continents, eroding away everything in their path.
paras.zh: 在侵蚀大陆上，冰川和冰盖比河流更有效率，即使在缓坡上也是如此。冰盖会慢慢地滑下山坡，穿过隆起的大陆，侵蚀掉沿途的一切。

paras.en: In contrast to Laurentia, Baltica and North China, we found that Australia and South America experienced only two cycles of uplift and subsidence from 900 million years ago. This scenario is not conducive to the formation and preservation of the Great Unconformity – and indeed we see little evidence of it on these continents.
paras.zh: 与劳伦大陆、波罗的海和华北相比，我们发现澳大利亚和南美洲自9亿年前以来仅经历了两次隆起和沉降周期。这种情况不利于大不整合面的形成和保存——事实上，我们在这些大陆上几乎看不到任何证据。

paras.en: Our research suggests the missing pages in Earth’s geological archive may be due to slow mantle convection that gently lifted entire continents then made them subside over hundreds of millions of years.
paras.zh: 我们的研究表明，地球地质档案中缺失的页面可能是由于缓慢的地幔对流造成的，这种对流轻轻地抬升了整个大陆，然后使它们在数亿年的时间里下沉。

paras.en: In that sense, the Great Unconformity is the fingerprint of deep Earth processes. Forces deep beneath our feet have left planet-scale marks in the geological record, and shaped the environment in which complex life first evolved.
paras.zh: 从这个意义上说，大不整合面是地球深层过程的指纹。我们脚下深处的力量在地质记录中留下了行星规模的痕迹，并塑造了复杂生命最初进化的环境。

paras.en: This article was first published by The Conversation. Read the original article here.
paras.zh: 本文最初由《对话》发表。在这里阅读原文。

articles.title: A drug-free diabetes treatment? An implant lowers blood sugar in mice
articles.author: Isha Ishtiaq

paras.en: A wireless implant that clears excess sugar from the blood could someday offer a drug-free way to treat type 2 diabetes and obesity.
paras.zh: 一种清除血液中多余糖分的无线植入物有一天可能会提供一种无需药物的方法来治疗 2 型糖尿病和肥胖症。

paras.en: In mice with both conditions, the under-the-skin device brought high blood sugar back to normal within 60 to 90 minutes of being switched on, researchers report October 22 in Science. After six weeks, the treated mice lost up to 10 percent of their body weight and had lower triglycerides, a type of fat in the blood.
paras.zh: 研究人员于 10 月 22 日在《科学》杂志上报道，在患有这两种情况的小鼠中，皮下装置在启动后 60 至 90 分钟内使高血糖恢复正常。六周后，接受治疗的小鼠体重减轻了 10%，甘油三酯（血液中的一种脂肪）也降低了。

paras.en: Diabetes affects about 830 million people worldwide. Conventional type 2 diabetes treatments like insulin and GLP-1 drugs require careful dosing. Even experimental diabetes-controlling implants still rely on the hormone insulin, which clears sugar from the bloodstream but doesn’t rid the body of it, says Martin Fussenegger, a bioengineer at ETH Zurich. The new implant instead removes glucose from the body without added drugs, genes or living cells.
paras.zh: 糖尿病影响全球约 8.3 亿人。胰岛素和 GLP-1 药物等传统 2 型糖尿病治疗需要谨慎给药。苏黎世联邦理工学院的生物工程师马丁·富森格 (Martin Fussenegger) 表示，即使是实验性的糖尿病控制植入物仍然依赖于胰岛素激素，胰岛素可以清除血液中的糖分，但不会消除体内的糖分。新的植入物可以从体内去除葡萄糖，无需添加药物、基因或活细胞。

paras.en: The 3-centimeter-long device contains a catalyst made of gold flakes and platinum particles on spongelike graphite. When electricity powers it, the catalyst converts glucose into gluconate, a compound that is easier for the kidneys to flush out in urine. With less glucose available for energy, the body may turn to its fat stores instead, Fussenegger and colleagues suspect. In mice, that shift showed up as higher blood levels of chemicals released when fat breaks down, such as ketones. “This system kind of targets the root cause, which is the energy surplus by glucose in the body,” Fussenegger says.
paras.zh: 这个3厘米长的装置包含由金片和铂颗粒在海绵状石墨上制成的催化剂。当电力为其提供动力时，催化剂将葡萄糖转化为葡萄糖酸盐，这种化合物更容易被肾脏从尿液中排出。富塞内格和同事怀疑，由于可用于提供能量的葡萄糖减少，身体可能会转而使用脂肪储存。在小鼠中，这种转变表现为脂肪分解时血液中释放的化学物质（例如酮）水平升高。 “这个系统的目标是根本原因，即体内葡萄糖的能量过剩，”富塞内格说。

paras.en: The implant works like an automatic sugar-removal system: A wearable glucose monitor detects high blood sugar levels and sends readings through a smartphone that switches the implant on. When levels return to a safer range, it switches off. The automated system ran for two weeks in eight mice. The catalyst itself remained able to convert glucose after up to three months under their skin, though the study didn’t establish how long the entire device would last.
paras.zh: 该植入物的工作原理类似于自动除糖系统：可穿戴式血糖监测仪可检测高血糖水平，并通过打开植入物的智能手机发送读数。当水平恢复到更安全的范围时，它就会关闭。该自动化系统在八只小鼠身上运行​​了两周。尽管该研究没有确定整个装置能持续多久，但催化剂本身在皮肤下放置三个月后仍然能够转化葡萄糖。

paras.en: And it’s still unknown how well the device would work in people. “This is a potentially promising method,” says David Klonoff, an endocrinologist at Sutter Mills-Peninsula Medical Center in Burlingame, Calif., who was not involved in the study. “But the risks are significant and must be carefully ruled out before it can be safely tested on humans.”
paras.zh: 目前还不清楚该设备在人体中的效果如何。 “这是一种潜在有前途的方法，”加利福尼亚州伯林格姆萨特米尔斯半岛医疗中心的内分泌学家戴维·克洛诺夫（David Klonoff）说，他没有参与这项研究。 “但风险很大，必须仔细排除，然后才能在人体上进行安全测试。”

paras.en: Researchers need to determine how much gluconate the kidneys can clear, Klonoff says. If it builds up, it could disrupt the body’s acid-base balance, causing symptoms such as nausea or confusion; excreting it could also deplete electrolytes such as sodium and potassium, he notes.
paras.zh: 克洛诺夫说，研究人员需要确定肾脏可以清除多少葡萄糖酸。如果它积聚起来，可能会破坏身体的酸碱平衡，导致恶心或神智不清等症状；他指出，排出体外还会消耗钠和钾等电解质。

paras.en: Scaling up the device is another challenge. Humans consume about 250 grams of carbohydrates daily, compared with two grams for mice, Klonoff estimates. Meeting that demand could require a much larger implant or multiple devices, he says. In a lab test, a larger device cleared nearly all glucose from about 5 liters of solution, roughly an adult’s blood volume, though not a full day’s glucose intake.
paras.zh: 扩大设备规模是另一个挑战。 Klonoff 估计，人类每天消耗约 250 克碳水化合物，而小鼠则为 2 克。他说，满足这一需求可能需要更大的植入物或多个设备。在一项实验室测试中，一台更大的设备几乎清除了大约 5 升溶液中的所有葡萄糖，这大约是一个成年人的血容量，但还不是一整天的葡萄糖摄入量。

paras.en: Fussenegger’s team plans to test the device in pigs and sheep before considering human trials. If proven safe and effective, it could offer an alternative to existing diabetes treatments and a new weight-loss option for people regardless of whether they have diabetes, he says.
paras.zh: 富塞内格的团队计划在考虑进行人体试验之前先在猪和羊身上测试该装置。他说，如果被证明安全有效，它可以为现有糖尿病治疗提供一种替代方案，并为人们提供新的减肥选择，无论他们是否患有糖尿病。

articles.title: Your voice can now say things you never said
articles.author: Laura Sanders

paras.en: AI technology can create realistic clones of people’s voices. The resulting proliferation of synthetic voices ushers in all sorts of new scenarios, good and bad. “Today, with nothing more than a keyboard and an internet connection, you can type, and you can get an image, a voice, a video of anything, [of] anybody doing or saying anything,” says Hany Farid, a computer scientist at Dartmouth University.
paras.zh: 人工智能技术可以创建真实的人声克隆。由此产生的合成声音的激增带来了各种新的场景，无论好坏。达特茅斯大学计算机科学家哈尼·法里德 (Hany Farid) 表示：“如今，只需键盘和互联网连接，你就可以打字，并且可以获得任何内容的图像、声音、视频，以及任何人所做或所说的任何事情。”

paras.en: Some of these voice clones are deeply meaningful to people, as in the cases of people who lost their ability to speak. But voice clones can also cause harm, as with scams and deepfakes. And some uses fall into murky gray zones, such as voice clones that “speak” after a person has passed away. What happens to a person’s digital voice after they’re gone?
paras.zh: 其中一些声音克隆对人们具有深远的意义，就像那些失去说话能力的人一样。但声音克隆也可能造成伤害，例如诈骗和深度伪造。有些用途属于灰色地带，例如在人去世后“说话”的声音克隆。一个人去世后，他的数字声音会怎样？

paras.en: In this episode of The Deep End: Talk to Me, hear more from Farid, as well as from a former hospital chaplain and AI researcher, and from Jules Rodriguez, a man who communicates with a voice clone. You’ll also hear about a choice Jules made about what will happen to his voice once he’s gone.
paras.zh: 在《深渊：与我交谈》的这一集中，您将听到法里德、前医院牧师和人工智能研究员以及通过声音克隆进行交流的朱尔斯·罗德里格斯的更多信息。您还会听到朱尔斯做出的选择，即他去世后他的声音会发生什么变化。

paras.en: Laura Sanders: What’s a voice you like to listen to?
paras.zh: 劳拉·桑德斯：你喜欢听什么声音？

paras.en: Kate Nilson: That is a great question. I hope my students don’t listen to this. I was having Snoop Dogg read their assignments to me the other day, just because I thought it was funny. But I don’t know if I would say that’s my favorite.
paras.zh: 凯特·尼尔森：这是一个很好的问题。我希望我的学生不要听这个。有一天，我让史努比狗狗给我读他们的作业，只是因为我觉得这很有趣。但我不知道我是否会说这是我的最爱。

paras.en: Sanders: That’s speech language pathologist and professor Kate Nilson. And if you’re wondering, this is a real, legitimate thing that anyone can do.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：那是言语病理学家兼教授凯特·尼尔森。如果你想知道，这是任何人都可以做的真实、合法的事情。

paras.en: Snoop Dogg audio: Vector mathematics. Think about a car trip. Your displacement from your starting point is a vector.
paras.zh: Snoop Dogg 音频：矢量数学。想想开车旅行。从起点开始的位移是一个向量。

paras.en: Snoop Dogg: I’m glad to be the voice of reason so you can focus better, understand more, and enjoy listening to the internet in the voice of Snoop Dogg.
paras.zh: Snoop Dogg：我很高兴成为理性的声音，这样您就可以更好地集中注意力，了解更多，并享受以 Snoop Dogg 的声音收听互联网。

paras.en: Sanders: Welcome to The Deep End, Talk To Me. In this episode, we’re stepping out of the lab and into the new digital world we all live in. We’re going to get into some of the good, bad and strange scenarios that come up when voices can be cloned and let loose in the world. Let’s talk about it.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：欢迎来到深渊，跟我谈谈。在这一集中，我们将走出实验室，进入我们都生活的新数字世界。我们将进入当声音可以被克隆并在世界上释放时出现的一些好的、坏的和奇怪的场景。我们来谈谈吧。

paras.en: [voices] Hey mom, can I tell you something? Hi. Do you want to talk? That added layer of it being you. Hello? Your voice. Hi. Your voice is you.
paras.zh: [声音] 嘿妈妈，我可以告诉你一件事吗？你好。你想说话吗？那增加的一层就是你。你好？你的声音。你好。你的声音就是你。

paras.en: Sanders: As we’ve heard in earlier episodes, ultra-realistic voice clones can be extremely meaningful to people who can no longer speak.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：正如我们在前几集中听到的那样，超现实的声音克隆对于无法说话的人来说非常有意义。

paras.en: Jules Rodriguez: So when I first heard my cloned voice, it felt like I reappeared. When my wife first heard it, she cried because of how close it sounded like me before I lost my voice. I knew of the potential of this technology at that moment.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯·罗德里格斯：所以当我第一次听到我的克隆声音时，感觉就像我重新出现了一样。当我妻子第一次听到这首歌时，她哭了，因为这听起来太像我失声之前的我了。那一刻我就知道了这项技术的潜力。

paras.en: Sanders: These digital copies of voices have restored connections to their loved ones.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这些声音的数字副本已经恢复了他们与亲人的联系。

paras.en: MA Fernandez: You know, the first thing he played for me, I was like chills all over.
paras.zh: MA Fernandez：你知道，他为我演奏的第一首曲子，我浑身发冷。

paras.en: Patrick Darling: The first time I performed with the AI voice, I was surprised how physically connected I felt with it.
paras.zh: 帕特里克·达林：我第一次用人工智能声音表演时，我很惊讶我与它的身体联系。

paras.en: Sanders: These voice clones have been transformative for people who have lost the ability to talk. But the existence of realistic digital copies of voices has effects that ripple farther out into society.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这些声音克隆对于那些失去说话能力的人来说是变革性的。但真实的声音数字副本的存在会对社会产生更深远的影响。

paras.en: Hany Farid: So here’s where sort of state of the art is. Today, with nothing more than a keyboard and an internet connection, you can type and you can get an image, a voice, a video of anything, anybody doing or saying anything.
paras.zh: Hany Farid：这就是最先进的地方。如今，只需键盘和互联网连接，您就可以打字，并且可以获得任何内容、任何人所做或所说的任何图像、声音、视频。

paras.en: Sanders: That’s Hany Farid. He’s a computer scientist at Dartmouth College and cofounder of Get Real Security, a firm that sorts real from fake. I called him to ask how these voice clones have changed our world.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：那是汉尼·法里德。他是达特茅斯学院的计算机科学家，也是 Get Real Security 的联合创始人，这是一家辨别真假的公司。我打电话给他，询问这些声音克隆如何改变了我们的世界。

paras.en: Farid: If you had asked me, I don’t know, five years ago, is this possible? I would say, yeah, maybe, but not anytime soon. And then all of a sudden, boom, it just came out of nowhere.
paras.zh: 法里德：如果你五年前问我，我不知道这可能吗？我会说，是的，也许吧，但不会很快。然后突然间，砰的一声，它就凭空出现了。

paras.en: Sanders: This shift happened in a very, very short amount of time, and it has big implications, both good and bad.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这种转变发生在非常非常短的时间内，它产生了巨大的影响，无论好坏。

paras.en: Farid: And so we are living in, I think, in equal parts an exciting time and a terrifying time, and somehow those are coexisting.
paras.zh: 法里德：我认为，我们生活在一个激动人心的时代和一个可怕的时代，而且不知何故，这些时代是共存的。

paras.en: Sanders: Farid tells me about some of his research, which asks people to decide whether something, like a voice or a video, is real.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：法里德向我介绍了他的一些研究，该研究要求人们判断某些事物（例如声音或视频）是否真实。

paras.en: Farid: My bread and butter is developing technologies to distinguish real from fake. And we work with media outlets and law enforcement and courts, et cetera. But one of the questions you always want to ask when you’re in my business is, well, do you need the mathematics and the computation? Just let somebody listen to it or look at it. And can they tell the difference?
paras.zh: Farid：我的面包和黄油正在开发区分真假的技术。我们与媒体、执法部门和法院等合作。但是，当你从事我的业务时，你总是想问的问题之一是，你需要数学和计算吗？只要让某人听或看即可。他们能分辨出区别吗？

paras.en: Sanders: It turns out they cannot. In laboratory tests, people can’t reliably say whether a voice they hear was created by a machine or by a real living, breathing person.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：事实证明他们不能。在实验室测试中，人们无法可靠地判断他们听到的声音是由机器发出的还是由真人发出的。

paras.en: Farid: It’s essentially like they’re flipping a coin.
paras.zh: Farid：这本质上就像他们在掷硬币。

paras.en: Sanders: But there’s another, even higher bar for voice clones to pass. That’s whether they can mimic a specific person well enough to slip by undetected.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：但是声音克隆还有另一个甚至更高的门槛。问题在于它们是否能够很好地模仿特定的人，从而在不被发现的情况下溜走。

paras.en: Farid: The other question too is what if I, for example, play a real voice sample of your voice, Laura, and then I clone your voice using my favorite AI cloning technology, and then I type something and I get you to say something, and I play those two samples to somebody, and I don’t ask them if it’s real/fake. I say, is this the same person? Is the AI not only able to make something that is natural, but is it identity preserving?
paras.zh: Farid：另一个问题是，如果我播放你声音的真实声音样本，劳拉，然后我使用我最喜欢的人工智能克隆技术克隆你的声音，然后我输入一些东西，让你说一些东西，然后我向某人播放这两个样本，我不会问他们是真是假。我说，这是同一个人吗？人工智能不仅能够制造出自然的东西，而且还能保留身份吗？

paras.en: Sanders: Okay, give it a try yourself. Is this the same person?
paras.zh: 桑德斯：好吧，你自己尝试一下。这是同一个人吗？

paras.en: [Sanders voice clone] And how about now? Is this the same person?
paras.zh: [桑德斯的声音克隆]现在怎么样？这是同一个人吗？

paras.en: Farid: And when you ask them, is it the same person? They say yes, which means the AI has figured out with roughly 20 seconds or so of your voice how to make their AI sound like you, which is mind-blowing.
paras.zh: Farid：当你问他们时，是同一个人吗？他们说是，这意味着人工智能已经通过你大约 20 秒左右的声音弄清楚了如何让他们的人工智能听起来像你，这令人兴奋。

paras.en: Sanders: In the earlier episodes of this season, you’ve heard examples of the good that’s been created by these technological leaps. In many cases, that good comes because these voices are both extremely realistic and extremely good at sounding like a specific person. People want their voice to sound like theirs.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在本季的前几集中，你已经听说过这些技术飞跃所创造的美好例子。在许多情况下，这种好处的出现是因为这些声音非常真实，而且非常擅长听起来像特定的人。人们希望自己的声音听起来像自己的。

paras.en: Farid: People with ALS can speak with what sounds like their voice. We’ve seen beautiful examples of that. Translation, right? We can now translate things in real time from any language and it’ll sound like you. I’ve made videos of myself speaking any language I want and it sounds like me, and it’s amazing. It’s really cool.
paras.zh: Farid：患有 ALS 的人可以用听起来像他们自己的声音说话。我们已经看到了这方面的美丽例子。翻译一下吧？我们现在可以实时翻译任何语言的内容，而且听起来就像您一样。我制作了自己说任何我想要的语言的视频，听起来就像我一样，这太棒了。真的很酷。

paras.en: Sanders: These new ways to connect are very impressive, but as with any technology, these powerful realistic auditory dupes can be repurposed to cause harm.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这些新的连接方式令人印象深刻，但与任何技术一样，这些强大的现实听觉欺骗可以被重新利用以造成伤害。

paras.en: Farid: Some pretty bad stuff’s happening, right? So let’s just go through a few of these. So first, you’re seeing massive types of fraud. Everything from romance scams to people calling parents and saying your kids have been taken, pay a ransom, to geopolitics. People are getting on calls with who they think are leaders of other countries, and it’s not. It’s a deepfake. It’s an AI-generated voice or face.
paras.zh: Farid：一些非常糟糕的事情正在发生，对吧？让我们来看看其中的一些。首先，您会看到大量类型的欺诈行为。从爱情骗局到人们打电话给父母并说你的孩子被带走了，要支付赎金，再到地缘政治。人们正在与他们认为是其他国家领导人的人通话，但事实并非如此。这是一个深度伪造。这是人工智能生成的声音或面孔。

paras.en: Sanders: What Farid is saying feels especially relevant right now. I’m recording this episode in the fall of 2026, and midterm elections in the U.S. are upon us. Political ads are everywhere. Some of these ads use deepfake audio and video to make opponents say or do things they never did. Here are a few recent examples of deepfakes compiled by the New York Times.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：法里德所说的话现在感觉特别有意义。我在 2026 年秋天录制这一集，美国中期选举即将到来。政治广告无处不在。其中一些广告使用深度伪造的音频和视频来让对手说或做他们从未做过的事情。以下是《纽约时报》最近整理的一些深度伪造的例子。

paras.en: [Audio] Hi, I’m Zohran Mamdani and I’m Kathy Hochul and together, we’re making New York, don’t say affordable. I’m voting for Hochul because she basically gave me an early retirement. They stopped prosecuting people for crime, so now I get to sit back and play Candy Crush all day. Is New York getting a little expensive? I’m Kathy Hochul, and I’ve got just the thing. Clinton lover, Trump hater.
paras.zh: [音频] 大家好，我是 Zohran Mamdani，我是 Kathy Hochul，我们一起打造纽约，更不用说负担得起了。我投票给 Hochul，因为她基本上让我提前退休。他们不再起诉犯罪分子，所以现在我可以坐下来玩一整天的《糖果粉碎传奇》。纽约是不是有点贵了？我是凯西·霍赫尔（Kathy Hochul），我就是这样。克林顿的爱人，特朗普的仇恨者。

paras.en: Farid: When you can steal somebody’s likeness, their voice, and their face, you can do some damage. We’re seeing people doing content credential resets at companies. They call up and say, oh, I’m employee X. Will you reset my credential? That’s how they’re now attacking companies. We’re seeing North Korean IT workers penetrating Fortune 500 companies by disguising their voices and their accents and their identities. So lots of bad things, and not unpredictably bad.
paras.zh: 法里德：当你可以窃取某人的肖像、声音和面孔时，你就可以造成一些损害。我们看到人们在公司进行内容凭证重置。他们打电话说，哦，我是员工 X。您能重置我的凭据吗？这就是他们现在攻击公司的方式。我们看到朝鲜 IT 员工通过掩饰声音、口音和身份渗透到财富 500 强公司。所以有很多坏事，但并不是不可预测的坏事。

paras.en: Sanders: There are romance scams, political scams, employment scams, money scams of all sorts. Farid was even involved in one himself.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：有爱情骗局、政治骗局、就业骗局、金钱骗局等等。法里德本人甚至也参与其中。

paras.en: Farid: My voice was cloned by an attacker. I was working a very sensitive case with an attorney. Not many people knew about it. And he got a call from my phone number in my voice talking about the case. And after about three minutes, got suspicious, hung up, called me back. Wasn’t me.
paras.zh: Farid：我的声音被攻击者克隆了。我正在和一位律师一起处理一个非常敏感的案件。没有多少人知道这件事。他接到了我的电话号码的电话，我的声音谈论着这个案子。大约三分钟后，我开始怀疑，挂断电话，给我回了电话。不是我。

paras.en: Sanders: With the proliferation of AI chatbots to write the scripts for these fake voices, these scams can be deployed on a very large scale. That means there’s no human in the loop except for the person getting scammed. There’s something depressing about the loss of this extremely personal information. And the worst part is that these cloned voices feel like they’re just the latest piece of privacy eroding.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：随着人工智能聊天机器人为这些虚假声音编写脚本的激增，这些骗局可以大规模部署。这意味着除了被骗的人之外，没有人参与其中。丢失这些极其个人的信息令人沮丧。最糟糕的是，这些克隆声音让人感觉它们只是最新的隐私侵蚀行为。

paras.en: Farid: For a long time, it was our social security numbers, our ability to access our bank accounts were held very tight. And then it’s like, all right, that’s over. Everybody’s got my social security. All the privacy problems of the last 20 years. So we’ve given up what we call PII, personally identifiable information. You can find my phone number, my address, my social security number, everything about me. And that’s true of almost every single American and every person in the world. All right, so that barrier was shattered, whatever, a few years ago. But then we held on to, okay, but I’ve got me, my voice, my likeness. Yeah, not so much. So now imagine that you have all the information you need about you, Laura, me, anybody, and now you can mimic me. Think about how powerful that is. And think about also how helpless I am. I have no control on the billions of calls unfolding every day, every hour, if somebody has co-opted my likeness.
paras.zh: 法里德：很长一段时间以来，我们的社会安全号码、我们访问银行账户的能力都受到严格控制。然后就好像，好吧，就这样结束了。每个人都有我的社会保障。过去 20 年的所有隐私问题。因此，我们放弃了所谓的 PII，即个人身份信息。你可以找到我的电话号码、我的地址、我的社会安全号码，以及关于我的一切。几乎每个美国人和世界上每个人都是如此。好吧，无论如何，几年前这个障碍就被打破了。但后来我们坚持了下来，好吧，但我有我自己，我的声音，我的肖像。是的，没那么多。现在想象一下，你拥有关于你、劳拉、我、任何人的所有信息，现在你可以模仿我。想想那有多么强大。也想想我是多么的无助。如果有人盗用了我的肖像，我无法控制每天、每小时发生的数十亿个电话。

paras.en: Sanders: Bigger picture, we’ve reached a point where it’s safe to say we can no longer automatically trust digital versions of other people. That applies to the images and sounds on my computer screen as I talked with Farid. Maybe this 2-D picture and sound coming from my laptop is a fake.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：从更大的角度来看，我们已经到了可以肯定地说我们不能再自动信任其他人的数字版本的地步。这适用于我与法里德交谈时电脑屏幕上的图像和声音。也许我笔记本电脑上发出的二维图像和声音是假的。

paras.en: Farid: So this two-dimensional version that you and I are sharing now, all right, I can’t control that. That can be stolen. The three-dimensional is right now still me, right? We don’t have the robots that can mimic us. Yet is the end of that sentence.
paras.zh: Farid：所以你和我现在分享的这个二维版本，好吧，我无法控制。那可以被盗。现在的三维还是我吧？我们没有可以模仿我们的机器人。然而这句话已经结束了。

paras.en: Sanders: So my interview with Farid was alarming. There are parallels here to any new technology, though. Today, people talk about brain rot from junk online. But remember that television was also going to rot our brains.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：所以我对法里德的采访令人震惊。不过，这与任何新技术都有相似之处。如今，人们谈论网络垃圾导致的大脑腐烂。但请记住，电视也会腐蚀我们的大脑。

paras.en: [Audio] Its content affects us. So does the sheer weight of the hours we watch.
paras.zh: [音频]它的内容影响着我们。我们观看的时间的绝对重量也是如此。

paras.en: Sanders: Phones today are the downfall of society, but actual wired telephones encountered really similar resistance when they first started appearing in homes.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：今天的电话是社会的衰落，但真正的有线电话在刚开始出现在家庭中时也遇到了类似的阻力。

paras.en: [Audio] In Chicago, Sharon Krall’s 15-year-old daughter Angie got so addicted to one teen talk line, she ran up an $850 bill in one month.
paras.zh: [音频] 在芝加哥，莎朗·克拉尔 (Sharon Krall) 15 岁的女儿安吉 (Angie) 沉迷于青少年谈话台词，一个月内就花光了 850 美元的账单。

paras.en: Sanders: No big technological advance has escaped this fear.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：任何重大的技术进步都无法逃脱这种恐惧。

paras.en: [Audio] We need teachers who are deeply concerned about how the modern media of communication are changing education.
paras.zh: [音频]我们需要深切关注现代传播媒体如何改变教育的教师。

paras.en: Sanders: Electricity, bicycles, railways, novels, even the printing press all had their skeptics. So this fear of the new thing has been around a long time. Are synthetic voices created by AI any different? Here’s Karina Nagin from Bridging Voice.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：电力、自行车、铁路、小说，甚至印刷机都有怀疑论者。所以这种对新事物的恐惧已经存在很长时间了。人工智能创建的合成声音有什么不同吗？这是来自 Bridging Voice 的卡琳娜·纳金 (Karina Nagin) 的报道。

paras.en: Nagin: Taking off my Bridging Voice hat and just as like a human being in the world, I think there’s a lot of things about AI that I’m very concerned. Deepfakes, the ability to make videos and audio that sound and look just like someone saying something that they’re not saying, I think is a huge, huge concern to our news and public information.
paras.zh: Nagin：摘下我的桥接语音帽子，就像世界上的人类一样，我认为人工智能有很多我非常关心的事情。 Deepfakes，即制作视频和音频听起来和看起来就像有人在说他们没有说的话的能力，我认为这是我们新闻和公共信息的一个巨大的担忧。

paras.en: Sanders: Nagin then pivots back to the good, the possibilities here.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：纳金然后回到好的方面，这里的可能性。

paras.en: Nagin: And then I put on my little hat in my space that I am like, this is how we can harness this to impact people’s lives in our space right now. And I think both conversations need to happen.
paras.zh: 纳金：然后我在我的空间里戴上我的小帽子，我想，这就是我们如何利用它来影响我们空间中人们的生活。我认为这两种对话都需要进行。

paras.en: Sanders: It occurs to me that I’m seeing the ends of the spectrum here. The stories Farid told me were awful. And the stories that Jules and Casey and others have told me were really, really life-changingly good. Yet these ends of the spectrum are the easy ones. The ones you can look at and say, that’s a horrible way to use this technology. Or that is a powerful and good way to use a voice clone. Between those two poles is the middle ground. That’s the place where Snoop explains cell biology.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我觉得我看到了这个范围的两端。法里德给我讲的故事很糟糕。朱尔斯、凯西和其他人告诉我的故事真的非常非常好，足以改变我的生活。然而，这些极端都是容易的。你可以看到并说，这是使用这项技术的可怕方式。或者说，这是使用语音克隆的一种强大且良好的方法。这两极之间是中间地带。这就是 Snoop 解释细胞生物学的地方。

paras.en: [Audio] The membrane separates the material outside the cell.
paras.zh: [音频] 膜将细胞外的物质分开。

paras.en: Sanders: Good, because it’s helping people learn more about mitochondria and who couldn’t use more of that in their lives. Bad, because Snoop never actually said those words, and it’s weird to pretend otherwise.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：很好，因为它可以帮助人们更多地了解线粒体，以及那些在生活中无法使用更多线粒体的人。糟糕的是，因为史努比实际上从未说过这些话，而且假装不这么说很奇怪。

paras.en: [Audio] The artists of the Renaissance said that man’s main concern should be for man.
paras.zh: [音频]文艺复兴时期的艺术家说，人的主要关心应该是为了人。

paras.en: Sanders: There are deepfakes of the late great physicist Richard Feynman delivering famous lectures.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：已故伟大物理学家理查德·费曼发表著名演讲的深度伪造品。

paras.en: [Audio] The problem is the laws of physics themselves. Let me start with something basic. The next star over from us is called Proxima Centauri.
paras.zh: [音频] 问题在于物理定律本身。让我从一些基本的事情开始。我们附近的下一颗恒星叫做比邻星。

paras.en: Sanders: Good because it introduces some amazing physics to people who would otherwise scroll past? Bad because it’s somewhat disrespectful and possibly inaccurate? There aren’t easy answers here. This murky middle gets even murkier with the invention of griefbots. Those are digital versions of people who have passed away. And that means that special voices can keep talking to us long after the body that created them is gone.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：很好，因为它向那些原本会滚动过去的人介绍了一些令人惊奇的物理学？不好是因为它有点不尊重而且可能不准确？这里没有简单的答案。随着悲伤机器人的发明，这个阴暗的中间变得更加阴暗。这些是已故之人的数字版本。这意味着特殊的声音可以在创造它们的身体消失很久之后继续与我们交谈。

paras.en: I read a poignant post online written by a guy who had lost his dad after years of dementia. He missed his dad’s voice, he wrote, so he cloned it. He paid for the starter pack, submitted three minutes of his dad’s audio, and he wrote, quote, a few minutes later, I had a scarily accurate clone of my dead father’s voice. He goes on to write, quote, my family and I had a good cathartic cry upon hearing the results. I had his cloned voice read the Lord’s Prayer as well as ‘Twas the Night before Christmas. Just hearing his simulated voice again is such a blessing and is helping me in the grief process. End quote.
paras.zh: 我在网上读到一篇令人心酸的帖子，作者是一位因多年痴呆症而失去父亲的人。他写道，他想念父亲的声音，所以他克隆了它。他支付了入门包的费用，提交了三分钟的他父亲的音频，然后他写道，几分钟后，我就得到了我已故父亲的声音的极其准确的克隆。他继续写道，引用，我和我的家人在听到结果后哭了一场。我让他的克隆声音朗读了主祷文以及《这是圣诞节前夜》。再次听到他的模拟声音真是一件幸事，并且正在帮助我度过悲伤的过程。结束报价。

paras.en: There are lots of companies now offering this exact thing. A casual search online gets me to a company that sells chats with dead loved ones. There’s a big orange button to click that says bring them back to life. A 2024 documentary called “Eternal You” follows the stories of people as they grapple with this idea. Here’s a little bit of the trailer.
paras.zh: 现在有很多公司提供这种产品。在网上随意搜索，我找到了一家销售与已故亲人聊天的公司。有一个橙色的大按钮可以点击，上面写着让它们复活。一部 2024 年的纪录片《永恒的你》讲述了人们与这个想法作斗争的故事。这是预告片的一小部分。

paras.en: [Audio] We are on the verge of a new era. Hi. It’s like, it’s the funniest thing. It’s like, what’s the first thing you say to someone that’s dead? Like, welcome back.
paras.zh: [音频]我们正处于新时代的边缘。你好。就像，这是最有趣的事情。就像，你对死去的人说的第一句话是什么？就像，欢迎回来。

paras.en: Sanders: Griefbots or digital avatars of loved ones offer a bridge from the past to the present, a way to remember vividly. But they are also a denial, of sorts, that all life must come to an end.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：悲伤机器人或亲人的数字化身提供了从过去到现在的桥梁，是一种生动地记住的方式。但它们也在某种程度上否认所有生命都必须结束。

paras.en: [Audio] And what I can tell you is that AI really is changing the way that we interact with death.
paras.zh: [音频]我可以告诉你的是，人工智能确实正在改变我们与死亡互动的​​方式。

paras.en: Sanders: That’s from a 2025 TEDx talk from Dylan Thomas Doyle. He’s a former hospital chaplain, current academic researcher at Northwestern University and self-described philosophy bro. His work explores death and AI.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这是迪伦·托马斯·道尔 2025 年 TEDx 演讲中的内容。他曾是一名医院牧师，现任西北大学学术研究员，自称是哲学兄弟。他的作品探索死亡和人工智能。

paras.en: [Audio] Imagine that you are at a funeral, and you’re sitting there in silent reflection, and all of a sudden, on the back screen in the auditorium, a woman’s face appears. And it’s the face of a woman named Marina. And her hologram, she starts talking to you, and she starts asking you how you’re doing today. And you answer her, and then you ask her a question back. And she responds as if she is still there.
paras.zh: [音频]想象一下，你正在参加一场葬礼，你坐在那里默默地沉思，突然，礼堂的后屏幕上出现了一张女人的脸。这是一个名叫玛丽娜的女人的脸。和她的全息图，她开始和你说话，她开始问你今天过得怎么样。你回答她，然后你反问她一个问题。她的反应就好像她还在那里一样。

paras.en: Sanders: I called Doyle to ask about the implications of using technology this way.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我打电话给多伊尔询问以这种方式使用技术的影响。

paras.en: Doyle: It was on my radar as a chaplain and a technology researcher, I started thinking through, well, what is the actual impact of this technology on people? So what is it like to hear the voice, in the context of this podcast, the voice of, say, your father who’s passed away while you’re actively grieving their death? And they’re not just repeating what they said or a journal entry in their voice, but like, creating new stories and new relationships through their voice. It gives a lot of people existential ick, is what I’ve heard. And that’s something that I really, I’m curious about.
paras.zh: 多伊尔：作为一名牧师和技术研究员，我开始思考这项技术对人们的实际影响是什么？那么，在这个播客的背景下，听到你的父亲的声音，比如说，当你正在积极哀悼他们的死亡时，听到他去世的声音是什么感觉？他们不仅仅是用自己的声音重复自己所说的话或日记条目，而是通过自己的声音创造新的故事和新的关系。据我所知，它让很多人感到厌恶。这确实是我很好奇的事情。

paras.en: Sanders: There’s tension here, Doyle tells me.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：多伊尔告诉我，这里存在紧张局势。

paras.en: Doyle: So there’s this push force where you’re like, this is not right. We don’t have the narrative or cultural script to understand what’s going on there. But then as people are beginning to use it, there’s a comfort that comes out of it. So we’re working in that tension space between this comfort that comes, then you’re still dealing with this push away from this technology of it just being weird in a way that people are still grappling with language, I think, to describe.
paras.zh: 多伊尔：所以你会觉得有一种推力，这是不对的。我们没有叙事或文化脚本来理解那里正在发生的事情。但当人们开始使用它时，就会产生一种安慰。因此，我们正在这种即将到来的舒适感之间的紧张空间中工作，然后你仍然在处理这种远离这项技术的情况，它只是以一种奇怪的方式，我认为，人们仍在努力用语言来描述。

paras.en: Sanders: It’s not clear how these types of interactions might affect grieving. They could help or they could hurt.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：目前尚不清楚这些类型的互动如何影响悲伤。他们可能会提供帮助，也可能会造成伤害。

paras.en: Doyle: There is this tension between more healthy continuing bonds. So continuing that relationship by, say, writing letters to your dead loved one or, you know, talking out loud to them and continuing that relationship in a positive way that moves us through a healthy grief process and a grief journey. Or hanging on to our relationship with that person to a degree where we can’t actually do any sort of moving on.
