paras.zh: 多伊尔：更健康的持续关系之间存在着这种紧张关系。因此，通过给死去的亲人写信，或者大声地与他们交谈，以积极的方式继续这种关系，让我们度过一个健康的悲伤过程和悲伤之旅，来继续这种关系。或者我们紧紧抓住与那个人的关系，以至于我们实际上无法采取任何行动。

paras.en: Sanders: Doyle points out that we don’t have good data on how many people might be using griefbots.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：多伊尔指出，我们没有关于有多少人可能使用悲伤机器人的良好数据。

paras.en: Doyle: I just don’t want us to get ahead of ourselves when it comes to people like using these. So the capability to do everything we’ve talked about with griefbots is there. But the actual use cases of individuals in their homes using this, it’s still pretty unclear about the adoption of those technologies.
paras.zh: 多伊尔：我只是不想让我们在谈到喜欢使用这些的人时表现得超前。因此，悲伤机器人有能力完成我们谈到的所有事情。但个人在家中使用该技术的实际用例，这些技术的采用情况仍然相当不清楚。

paras.en: Sanders: But even if griefbots aren’t widespread, the questions they raise aren’t going away. These voices are blurring the lines between a memory and a present-day experience, between alive and dead. Here’s Karina Nagin again.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：但即使悲伤机器人并不普遍，它们提出的问题也不会消失。这些声音模糊了记忆与当下经历、生与死之间的界限。卡琳娜·纳金又来了。

paras.en: Nagin: It’s an interesting conversation that we’re having right now of what happens to your voice once you pass away. Some people are starting to integrate this into their wills or their sort of final wishes of, do you want your voice to be able to speak at your own memorial service?
paras.zh: 纳金：我们现在正在进行一场有趣的对话，内容是关于你去世后你的声音会发生什么。有些人开始将其融入他们的遗嘱或最终愿望中，你希望你的声音能够在你自己的追悼会上发言吗？

paras.en: Do you want to have messages saved in your voice that are for your child at graduation that they listen to? Who and when can use that? I think that these are things that people are starting to think about. Who owns your voice? Can your children use your voice to write a speech for their children’s graduation? Or do you want that voice to be deleted once you pass away? Very tricky questions.
paras.zh: 您是否想在您的声音中保存留言供您的孩子在毕业典礼上聆听？谁以及何时可以使用它？我认为这些是人们开始思考的事情。谁拥有你的声音？您的孩子可以用您的声音为孩子的毕业典礼写演讲稿吗？或者你希望在你去世后删除那个声音？非常棘手的问题。

paras.en: Sanders: Rules about who can use voice clones are all over the place. Regulations vary by state and by country, and even companies have their own individual policies in place. There are no clear guidelines, and that makes sense given how young this technology is. Conversations about digital voices and how to use them are inherently very personal. There are as many different takes as there are people. I asked MA if she and Jules had talked about this.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：关于谁可以使用语音克隆的规则无处不在。法规因州和国家而异，甚至公司也有自己的个人政策。目前还没有明确的指导方针，考虑到这项技术还很年轻，这是有道理的。关于数字语音以及如何使用它们的对话本质上是非常个人化的。有多少人就有多少种不同的看法。我问妈妈她和朱尔斯是否谈过这件事。

paras.en: MA: I love that question. Both of us love this question because it’s so important. And we talked about it before he got the trache. Like when he was already using the voice, we were talking about different things in bed at night. And he said, you know, I have a very clear request that my voice like dies with me, basically, that, you know, I ask that you don’t use the voice to keep me alive in any way, that there’s no… And I was like, 100 percent clear. I hadn’t even thought about that. But yeah, it would make sense to be like, I miss him so much. I want to, whatever or. But no, as far as we’re concerned, his voice dies when he does. And his voice will live on in whatever videos or things we captured, whatever he’s left us intentionally. And that’s as far as that goes.
paras.zh: MA：我喜欢这个问题。我们俩都喜欢这个问题，因为它非常重要。在他接受气管切开术之前我们就讨论过这件事。就像当他已经使用这个声音时，我们晚上在床上谈论不同的事情。他说，你知道，我有一个非常明确的要求，我的声音会随着我一起消失，基本上，你知道，我要求你不要以任何方式使用声音让我活下去，没有……我的感觉是百分百清楚。我什至没有想到这一点。但是，是的，我非常想念他，这是有道理的。我想要，无论如何。但不，就我们而言，当他这样做时，他的声音就消失了。他的声音将永远存在于我们拍摄的任何视频或事物中，无论他故意留给我们什么。就这样了。

paras.en: Sanders: So when Jules is gone, his voice will be gone too. But right now is a different story.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：所以当朱尔斯去世时，他的声音也会消失。但现在情况不同了。

paras.en: MA: Well back in 2021, I was writing an Instagram post about something. It was him playing with Skylar in the backyard while he was already like, you know, had trouble with everything, but he was doing what he could. And I asked him like, you know, what, what do you want to caption it? And he just said that, right here, right now phrase, something else, and like right here, right now. And it became our family mantra. It became something that we wanted to just to share and in both a sense of like do the things that you want to do.
paras.zh: MA：早在 2021 年，我就在 Instagram 上写了一篇关于某事的帖子。那是他和斯凯拉在后院玩耍，而他已经好像，你知道，一切都遇到了麻烦，但他正在尽力而为。我问他，你知道，你想给它加上什么标题吗？他只是说，就在这里，现在，短语，其他的东西，就像就在这里，现在。这成了我们家庭的座右铭。它成为我们想要分享的东西，从某种意义上说，就像做你想做的事情。

paras.en: And also something that’s always been big for Jules that I’ve admired him articulate is that it’s not just about, oh, just go forward and do all the things and like suck the marrow out of life. It’s like just also, like, settle. Like it doesn’t have to be that extreme, you know. There’s a beautiful thing about that presence and that settling in. And again, with ALS being something where you’re given the diagnosis, which is terminal, it’s basically a death sentence. Most people are given, you know, two to five years. You don’t know where you’re going to fall in that. We’ve known people that have passed away in a year and a half. We’ve known people that are six years in like Jules, but can still kind of walk around, speak a little bit. ALS touches everybody really differently. So you really don’t know what’s coming. And there’s a lot of like forward thinking that you can do that detaches you from being in your life. So how are you here? And then there’s a lot of backwards, you know, reminiscing and grieving about all the things we’ve lost and how we wish things were different. But then that also takes you out of like this moment right now and this part of your story.
paras.zh: 对朱尔斯来说，我很钦佩他能表达出来的一直很重要的一点是，这不仅仅是，哦，继续前进，做所有的事情，就像从生活中吸取骨髓一样。这就像也，就像，安顿下来。你知道，事情不必那么极端。这种存在和安定下来是一件美好的事情。再说一次，当你被诊断出 ALS 时，这是晚期的，基本上就等于被判了死刑。你知道，大多数人都会被给予两到五年的时间。你不知道自己会陷入其中。我们认识一年半内去世的人。我们认识像朱尔斯这样六岁的人，但仍然可以四处走动，说一点话。 ALS 对每个人的影响确实不同。所以你真的不知道会发生什么。你可以做很多类似的前瞻性思考，让你脱离生活。那么你在这里怎么样？然后有很多倒退，你知道，回忆和悲伤我们失去的所有东西，以及我们如何希望事情有所不同。但这也会让你脱离现在的这一刻和故事的这一部分。

paras.en: Sanders: This part of the story is the important part. Right here, right now.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：故事的这一部分是重要的部分。就在这里，就是现在。

paras.en: On the next and final episode of The Deep End, Talk to Me. We’re going to look at what’s next for Jules and Casey and what’s next for the science racing to give voices back to people.
paras.zh: 在《深渊》的下一集也是最后一集中，《跟我说话》。我们将看看朱尔斯和凯西的下一步是什么，以及科学竞赛的下一步是什么，以回馈人们的声音。

paras.en: Vikash Gilja: We can see all the pieces coming together. All of the emphasis, capital, quite frankly, talent focused on advancing AI techniques and technologies. You know, our little corner can benefit from it, right? These tools weren’t available even five years ago.
paras.zh: Vikash Gilja：我们可以看到所有的部分都整合在一起。所有的重点、资本、坦率地说、人才都集中在推进人工智能技术和技术上。你知道，我们的小角落可以从中受益，对吗？这些工具在五年前还没有出现。

paras.en: Sanders: What’s next for the human voice?
paras.zh: 桑德斯：人声的下一步是什么？

paras.en: Samantha Brosler: Of course, ultimately, we’re hoping to expand this to even larger vocabulary and more range of body movements across the whole body to help allow people more expression in their communication.
paras.zh: Samantha Brosler：当然，最终我们希望将其扩展到更大的词汇量和更多范围的全身身体动作，以帮助人们在交流中更多地表达。

paras.en: This is The Deep End, Talk to Me. I’m Laura Sanders. If you like this podcast tell your friends and leave us a review. It helps the show a lot. Send us your questions and your comments at podcasts@sciencenews.org.
paras.zh: 这是深渊，跟我说话。我是劳拉·桑德斯。如果您喜欢这个播客，请告诉您的朋友并给我们留下评论。对节目帮助很大。请通过 podcasts@sciencenews.org 将您的问题和意见发送给我们。

paras.en: Sanders: The Deep End is a production of Science News. It’s based on original reporting by me, Laura Sanders. This episode was produced and mixed by Ella Rowen. Our project manager is Ashley Yeager. Nancy Shute is our editor in chief. Our music is by Blue Dot Sessions. The podcast is made possible in part by the Burroughs Wellcome Fund with support from PRX.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：深渊是《科学新闻》的制作。它基于我劳拉·桑德斯的原创报道。本集由 Ella Rowen 制作和混音。我们的项目经理是阿什利·耶格尔。南希·舒特是我们的主编。我们的音乐是由 Blue Dot Sessions 制作的。该播客的部分制作是由 Burroughs Wellcome 基金在 PRX 的支持下完成的。

paras.zh: 声音来源：Garuda1982 的《春天有自行车和乌鸦的城市公园》、kyles 的印刷机纺轮.flac、AudioSea 的 Turning Pages 01.wav。

articles.title: Record-low temperature created on China’s space station
articles.author: Emily Conover

paras.en: This is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback?
paras.zh: 这是一个由人工智能配音的人类书写的故事。有反馈吗？

paras.en: Science has reached a new low. Temperature, that is.
paras.zh: 科学已经达到了新的低点。温度，就是。

paras.en: Scientists cooled a collection of atoms to about 10 picokelvins, or 10 trillionths of a kelvin. That’s barely a smidge above absolute zero (−273.15° Celsius). The atoms formed a Bose-Einstein condensate, a quantum state of matter, colder than any before, researchers report November 5 in Science.
paras.zh: 科学家将一组原子冷却至约 10 皮开尔文，即万亿分之一开尔文。这仅比绝对零（-273.15°摄氏度）高一点点。研究人员于 11 月 5 日在《科学》杂志上报道称，这些原子形成了玻色-爱因斯坦凝聚体，这是一种物质的量子态，其温度比以前任何时候都要低。

paras.en: To achieve that record-low chill, scientists took their work to space. The atoms orbited Earth aboard China’s Tiangong space station. There, researchers used laser-based traps to contain 20,000 rubidium atoms and reduce their motion, thereby cooling them. At an atomic level, temperature is tied to motion: Atoms and molecules in the air around us move more slowly when it’s colder. Similarly, in systems of cold atoms, scientists can define an effective temperature based on how slowly the atoms spread apart when they are allowed to expand.
paras.zh: 为了实现创纪录的最低寒冷，科学家们将他们的工作带到了太空。这些原子乘坐中国天宫空间站绕地球运行。在那里，研究人员使用基于激光的陷阱来容纳 20,000 个铷原子并减少它们的运动，从而冷却它们。在原子层面上，温度与运动有关：当温度较低时，我们周围空气中的原子和分子运动得更慢。同样，在冷原子系统中，科学家可以根据原子膨胀时扩散的速度来定义有效温度。

paras.en: On Earth, gravitational forces cause clouds of atoms to sag, reducing the effectiveness of cooling. But on the space station, the atoms experienced microgravity, the apparent weightlessness of an object in free fall.
paras.zh: 在地球上，重力会导致原子云下垂，从而降低冷却效率。但在空间站上，原子经历了微重力，即自由落体物体表面上的失重状态。

paras.en: To make a Bose-Einstein condensate, a disorderly gaggle of atoms is cooled until the atoms all take on the same quantum state, acting as one entity. By experimenting with ultracold atoms, researchers can study exotic states of matter and other mysterious physics. And they can test fundamental concepts, such as the equivalence principle — the idea that explains why objects of different masses fall at the same rate in a vacuum.
paras.zh: 为了制造玻色-爱因斯坦凝聚体，一群无序的原子被冷却，直到所有原子都呈现相同的量子态，充当一个实体。通过对超冷原子进行实验，研究人员可以研究奇异的物质状态和其他神秘的物理现象。他们还可以测试基本概念，例如等效原理——该原理解释了为什么不同质量的物体在真空中以相同的速度下落。

paras.en: Spacefaring Bose-Einstein condensates were previously made on the International Space Station, at effective temperatures as low as 52 picokelvins. And an experiment on Earth, in which atoms were dropped down a tower to induce weightlessness, reached 38 picokelvins. But drop tower experiments are limited by the time their free fall lasts. That’s not an issue for experiments in Earth’s orbit. So cold atoms in space are really taking off.
paras.zh: 太空玻色-爱因斯坦凝聚体之前是在国际空间站上制造的，有效温度低至 52 皮开尔文。在地球上进行的一项实验中，原子从塔上落下以产生失重状态，温度达到了 38 皮开尔文。但落塔实验受到自由落体持续时间的限制。对于地球轨道上的实验来说，这不是问题。所以太空中的冷原子确实正在起飞。

articles.title: A Stinky Gas Seeping From The Bowels of Mars May Reveal The Planet Is Still Volcanically Active
articles.author: Ivan Farkas

paras.en: Mars has undergone some monumental PR shifts over the past few centuries.
paras.zh: 在过去的几个世纪里，火星经历了一些巨大的公关转变。

paras.en: Once thought to be criss-crossed with canals created by an untold alien race, it has since been reclassified as still red but overwhelmingly dead.
paras.zh: 曾经被认为与一个不为人知的外星种族所创造的运河纵横交错，它已被重新分类为仍​​然是红色的，但绝大多数已经死亡。

paras.en: Newer research has shown our smaller neighbor was once tantalizingly watery and habitable, and we now know it's all sorts of active, awash in green aurorae (which we may one day personally glimpse), surprisingly recent lava flows, and some real rattling marsquakes.
paras.zh: 最新的研究表明，我们较小的邻居曾经水汪汪、适宜居住，现在我们知道它正处于各种活跃状态，充满了绿色的极光（有一天我们可能会亲眼目睹），令人惊讶的是最近的熔岩流，以及一些真正的火星地震。

paras.en: Now, the detection of some stinky gas suggests its heart (or gut) is still beating with melty magma.
paras.zh: 现在，检测到一些恶臭气体表明它的心脏（或肠道）仍在融化的岩浆中跳动。

paras.en: In a new study published in Science Advances, astronomers using the European Space Agency's (ESA) ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter (TGO) have reported detecting noxious hydrogen chloride (HCl) wafting around Alba Mons, the largest volcano (by surface area) on Mars.
paras.zh: 在《科学进展》杂志上发表的一项新研究中，天文学家使用欧洲航天局 (ESA) 的 ExoMars 微量气体轨道飞行器 (TGO) 报告称，检测到火星上最大的火山阿尔巴蒙斯 (按表面积计算) 周围飘荡着有毒的氯化氢 (HCl)。

paras.en: Their discovery hints that our neighbor is still magmatically active in its interior.
paras.zh: 他们的发现暗示我们的邻居的内部岩浆仍然活跃。

paras.en: "Our results are best explained by ongoing igneous processes in the Martian interior," the researchers say in the study.
paras.zh: 研究人员在研究中表示：“我们的结果最好地解释为火星内部正在进行的火成岩过程。”

paras.en: A process known as the chlorine cycle occurs on Earth as well, beginning during the early days of planetary formation as chlorine escapes from the interior, and is then fed by subsequent volcanism.
paras.zh: 地球上也发生了一种被称为氯循环的过程，该过程始于行星形成的早期，当时氯从内部逸出，然后通过随后的火山活动得到补充。

paras.en: Since chlorine is mobile and readily dissolved, it gets around significantly, 'hooking up' with, and being recycled within, numerous materials like sediments, water, permafrost, and ice clouds.
paras.zh: 由于氯具有流动性且易于溶解，因此它可以显着地四处流动，与沉积物、水、永久冻土和冰云等众多物质“结合”并在其中循环利用。

paras.en: It's known that Mars was very volcanically active in its adolescence, 3.7 to 3 billion years ago, during its Hesperian era, and later forged the biggest volcanoes in the Solar System, including Olympus Mons – which itself may have shown recent activity only around two million years ago.
paras.zh: 众所周知，火星在其青春期，即 3.7 至 30 亿年前的西斯皮利亚时代，火山活动非常活跃，后来形成了太阳系中最大的火山，包括奥林匹斯山——它本身可能仅在大约 200 万年前才显示出最近的活动。

paras.en: Multiple regions of the red planet show signs of recent volcanic activity over the past tens of millions of years, and hot mantle plumes could be melting parts of the Martian interior even today.
paras.zh: 这颗红色星球的多个区域显示出过去几千万年来近期火山活动的迹象，即使在今天，炽热的地幔羽流也可能正在融化火星内部的部分区域。

paras.en: Yet thermal signatures, surface features, and sulfurous gases and their products have remained hard to come by or inconclusive.
paras.zh: 然而，热特征、表面特征、二氧化硫气体及其产物仍然难以获得或尚无定论。

paras.en: Enter HCl, which continues to seep from magma even after eruptions have ended. Elevated chlorine ratios, compared to Earth, have also been detected in Martian meteorites, rocks, and regolith.
paras.zh: 即使在火山喷发结束后，HCl 仍会继续从岩浆中渗出。与地球相比，在火星陨石、岩石和风化层中也检测到氯含量较高。

paras.en: The researchers report multiple HCl detections above fissured ground near the Alba Mons volcano in Mars' northern Tharsis Plateau, a region of recent, perhaps even ongoing subterranean activity.
paras.zh: 研究人员报告称，在火星北部塔尔西斯高原阿尔巴蒙斯火山附近的裂缝地面上检测到了多次氯化氢，该地区最近甚至可能正在进行地下活动。

paras.en: Scientists have detected many HCl signals across Mars at various seasons of the Martian year, but many of these seem to be associated with Mars' hydrological and atmospheric processes.
paras.zh: 科学家们在火星年的不同季节在火星上检测到了许多 HCl 信号，但其中许多信号似乎与火星的水文和大气过程有关。

paras.en: However, a handful of HCl signals seem to seep from within the planet's potentially still-molten bowels. These intriguing signals appear in early summer in the northern hemisphere, when Mars is near aphelion, its farthest point from the Sun.
paras.zh: 然而，一些 HCl 信号似乎从地球可能仍处于熔化状态的内部渗透出来。这些有趣的信号出现在北半球初夏，此时火星位于距太阳最远的远日点附近。

paras.en: This northern summer is different from the southern summer. It's colder, and the atmosphere is clearer of dust and water vapor. This means that the HCl signals are more likely to be of magmatic origin, rather than the result of atmospheric aerosols. Accordingly, they do appear to emanate at lower altitudes.
paras.zh: 这个北方的夏天与南方的夏天不同。天气更冷了，大气中的灰尘和水蒸气也更加清晰。这意味着 HCl 信号更有可能是岩浆起源，而不是大气气溶胶的结果。因此，它们似乎确实是在较低的高度发出的。

paras.en: The early summer warming sublimates the overlying ice, allowing the HCl to escape from cracks leading to the Martian interior, which may otherwise be frozen over during cold snaps that plunge to -120 degrees Celsius (-184 degrees Fahrenheit).
paras.zh: 初夏变暖使覆盖的冰升华，使 HCl 从通往火星内部的裂缝中逸出，否则火星内部可能会在骤降至 -120 摄氏度（-184 华氏度）的寒流中被冻结。

paras.en: "The Trace Gas Orbiter was able to find the smoking gun. It was like looking for a needle in a haystack," explains co-lead author Daniel Mège, a planetary scientist at the Space Research Centre of the Polish Academy of Sciences.
paras.zh: “痕量气体轨道飞行器能够找到确凿的证据。这就像大海捞针一样，”共同主要作者、波兰科学院空间研究中心的行星科学家丹尼尔·梅格（Daniel Mège）解释道。

paras.en: "It's truly amazing that it spotted a handful of molecules from a perhaps intermittent source, whilst moving continuously along its orbit to monitor the whole Martian atmosphere."
paras.zh: “这确实令人惊奇，它从一个可能是间歇性的来源中发现了一些分子，同时沿着其轨道连续移动以监测整个火星大气层。”

paras.en: Indeed, these stinky signals are thin, with ghost-like concentrations in parts per billion. This is like picking the single pear jellybean from a sea of a billion licorice-flavored ones, possibly overturned during a factory-floor fiasco – or one drop of ink in a 10,000-gallon swimming pool.
paras.zh: 事实上，这些臭味信号很薄弱，浓度就像幽灵一样，只有十亿分之几。这就像从十亿甘草口味的梨糖豆中挑选一颗梨糖豆，可能在工厂车间的惨败中被打翻，或者在 10,000 加仑的游泳池中取出一滴墨水。

paras.en: The researchers advance three potential non-atmospheric causes for the HCl detections.
paras.zh: 研究人员提出了 HCl 检测的三个潜在的非大气原因。

paras.en: First, they could be of deep volcanic origin.
paras.zh: 首先，它们可能源自深层火山。

paras.en: Second, they could be due to mud volcanoes, which may release HCl as they bubble from the planetary bowels if they interact with magma, again supporting a volcanic source.
paras.zh: 其次，它们可能是由于泥火山造成的，如果泥火山与岩浆相互作用，它们从行星内部冒泡时可能会释放出HCl，这再次支持了火山源。

paras.en: Third, they may be explained by decomposition of chlorine-containing compounds on the surface.
paras.zh: 第三，它们可以通过表面上含氯化合物的分解来解释。

paras.en: However, the researchers say that a local, igneous source may provide the best explanation.
paras.zh: 然而，研究人员表示，当地的火成岩来源可能提供最好的解释。

paras.en: Especially as the HCl is linked to small fissures that sometimes form "swarms" stretching for tens of kilometers, occasionally ringed with dark-colored halos, perhaps similar to those around fumaroles on Earth.
paras.zh: 特别是由于氯化氢与小裂缝有关，这些裂缝有时会形成绵延数十公里的“群”，偶尔会环绕着深色光晕，可能类似于地球上喷气孔周围的光晕。

paras.en: If not for something maintaining these fissures, they would have disappeared eons ago under accumulating dust or seasonal landscape deformations. Intriguingly, they may be the chimneys of hydrothermal systems connected to a "volcanic plumbing system" deep within Mars.
paras.zh: 如果没有什么东西维持这些裂缝，它们早就在灰尘堆积或季节性景观变形的作用下消失了。有趣的是，它们可能是与火星深处的“火山管道系统”相连的热液系统的烟囱。

paras.en: Of course, this has implications for the most essential question of all, as melting magmas could provide heat and nutrients for extraterrestrials.
paras.zh: 当然，这对最重要的问题有影响，因为融化的岩浆可以为外星人提供热量和营养。

paras.en: "Looking for Martian life in the seeping fissures of the Alba Mons region would make a lot of sense," Mège concludes.
paras.zh: 梅格总结道：“在阿尔巴蒙斯地区的渗漏裂缝中寻找火星生命是很有意义的。”

paras.en: "If hydrothermal systems are active, they could contain the ingredients and energy needed for microorganisms to develop, and shield microorganisms from the hostile and changing environment above the surface."
paras.zh: “如果热液系统活跃，它们可能含有微生物发育所需的成分和能量，并保护微生物免受地表上方恶劣和不断变化的环境的影响。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Science Advances.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《科学进展》上。

articles.title: Treating Sleep Apnea Could Improve Sperm Quality, Study Finds
articles.author: Carly Cassella

paras.en: A lack of oxygen during sleep isn't just a problem for the lungs or the brain – it may also impact testicular function.
paras.zh: 睡眠期间缺氧不仅是肺部或大脑的问题，还可能影响睾丸功能。

paras.en: A small prospective study has now found that while obstructive sleep apnea is not associated with erectile dysfunction, it is associated with poorer sperm quality.
paras.zh: 一项小型前瞻性研究现已发现，虽然阻塞性睡眠呼吸暂停与勃起功能障碍无关，但与精子质量较差有关。

paras.en: When researchers compared 72 reproductive-aged men with untreated sleep apnea to 22 healthy controls, they found that patients with a sleep disorder demonstrated a significantly lower semen volume.
paras.zh: 当研究人员将 72 名未经治疗的睡眠呼吸暂停的育龄男性与 22 名健康对照者进行比较时，他们发现患有睡眠障碍的患者的精液量明显较低。

paras.en: Their semen also contained fewer sperm capable of swimming forward, and it showed elevated levels of several inflammatory markers.
paras.zh: 他们的精液中能够向前游动的精子也较少，而且几种炎症标记物的水平也有所升高。

paras.en: The findings, published in Sleep Medicine, suggest that disrupted sleep and a lack of oxygen at nighttime may be linked to higher sperm immobility.
paras.zh: 发表在《睡眠医学》上的研究结果表明，睡眠中断和夜间缺氧可能与精子活动度较高有关。

paras.en: This may or may not affect a person's ability to conceive, but as the study authors point out, these measures are "key determinants of male reproductive potential."
paras.zh: 这可能会也可能不会影响一个人的受孕能力，但正如研究作者指出的那样，这些措施是“男性生殖潜力的关键决定因素”。

paras.en: The good news is that when 25 participants in the study were treated with a CPAP machine (Continuous Positive Airway Pressure), they began to show improvements in progressive sperm motility as early as 1 month later.
paras.zh: 好消息是，当研究中的 25 名参与者接受 CPAP 机（持续气道正压通气）治疗时，他们早在 1 个月后就开始表现出精子活力的改善。

paras.en: "CPAP therapy is accompanied by longitudinal improvements in sperm motility," the authors explain, "suggesting that evaluation for sleep-disordered breathing may be considered an exploratory assessment in men presenting with unexplained semen abnormalities."
paras.zh: 作者解释说：“CPAP 治疗伴随着精子活力的纵向改善，这表明对睡眠呼吸障碍的评估可以被视为对出现不明原因精液异常的男性的探索性评估。”

paras.en: Obstructive sleep apnea occurs when the airway becomes restricted during sleep, leading to loud snoring that's interrupted by pauses in breathing.
paras.zh: 当睡眠期间气道受到限制时，就会发生阻塞性睡眠呼吸暂停，导致打鼾声很大，并被呼吸暂停打断。

paras.en: It impacts about a quarter of all men over the age of 30, and it does more than leave people feeling unrefreshed. Patients with this sleep disorder are more likely to develop high blood pressure and other cardiovascular concerns.
paras.zh: 它影响了大约四分之一的 30 岁以上男性，而且它的作用不仅仅是让人们感到精神不振。患有这种睡眠障碍的患者更有可能出现高血压和其他心血管问题。

paras.en: In the past, observational studies have found that sleep apnea is linked to a higher risk of erectile dysfunction, and yet there is scarce evidence on how sperm might be affected.
paras.zh: 过去，观察性研究发现睡眠呼吸暂停与勃起功能障碍的较高风险有关，但很少有证据表明精子可能受到影响。

paras.en: In 2025, urologists in Brazil penned a correspondence for Nature Reviews Urology that argued sleep medicine should be part of a routine evaluation for male infertility.
paras.zh: 2025 年，巴西的泌尿科医生为 Nature Reviews Urology 撰写了一封信函，认为睡眠医学应该成为男性不育症常规评估的一部分。

paras.en: Animal studies and some observational human studies suggest that a lack of oxygen or systemic inflammation, triggered by sleep apnea, could possibly mess with sperm production.
paras.zh: 动物研究和一些人类观察研究表明，睡眠呼吸暂停引发的缺氧或全身炎症可能会扰乱精子的产生。

paras.en: This new study, led by researchers at the University of Hong Kong–Shenzhen Hospital in China, is small and the treatment was not randomized, but the authors say it explores a "critical knowledge gap" that is "largely unexplored".
paras.zh: 这项由中国香港大学深圳医院的研究人员领导的新研究规模较小，治疗也不是随机的，但作者表示，它探索了一个“很大程度上尚未探索”的“关键知识差距”。

paras.en: Male participants in the study were aged 18 to 50, and some were diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea using an overnight test at a sleep center.
paras.zh: 该研究的男性参与者年龄在 18 岁至 50 岁之间，其中一些人通过睡眠中心的夜间测试被诊断患有阻塞性睡眠呼吸暂停。

paras.en: Compared to those without sleep apnea, researchers found that those with sleep apnea had lower semen quality, independent of erectile function.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，与没有睡眠呼吸暂停的人相比，患有睡眠呼吸暂停的人精液质量较低，与勃起功能无关。

paras.en: Participants in the sleep apnea group had roughly 10 percent fewer sperm capable of swimming forward and 10 percent fewer sperm capable of swimming at all.
paras.zh: 睡眠呼吸暂停组的参与者中能够向前游动的精子大约减少了 10%，而能够游动的精子则减少了 10%。

paras.en: During follow-up, 25 participants used a CPAP regularly for four hours or more per night on five or more nights a week.
paras.zh: 在随访期间，25 名参与者每周定期使用 CPAP 呼吸机 5 晚或以上，每晚 4 小时或以上。

paras.en: One month later, researchers noticed that in men who used the CPAP machine, the percentage of progressively motile sperm increased from nearly 40 percent to 45 percent.
paras.zh: 一个月后，研究人员注意到，使用 CPAP 机器的男性中，逐渐活动的精子百分比从近 40% 增加到 45%。

paras.en: No significant reductions were reported in the four elevated inflammatory markers.
paras.zh: 据报道，四种升高的炎症标志物没有显着降低。

paras.en: At three months, only 15 men were still using the CPAP machine and reporting for follow-up analysis. By six months, only 8 men remained in the trial.
paras.zh: 三个月后，只有 15 名男性仍在使用 CPAP 机器并报告后续分析。六个月后，试验中只剩下 8 名男子。

paras.en: This large drop-out rate makes it difficult to evaluate long-term success.
paras.zh: 如此高的辍学率使得很难评估长期的成功。

paras.en: CPAP machines are clunky and uncomfortable, and many patients with sleep apnea find them difficult to use in the long run.
paras.zh: CPAP 机笨重且不舒服，许多患有睡眠呼吸暂停的患者发现从长远来看很难使用它们。

paras.en: Among those who persisted with treatment, however, sperm motility stayed above baseline; though as the sample size was small, the researchers caution against reading too much into it.
paras.zh: 然而，在那些坚持接受治疗的人中，精子活力仍保持在基线以上。尽管样本量很小，研究人员警告不要过度解读。

paras.en: "Taken together, these findings support a conceptual model in which sleep-disordered breathing and local seminal microenvironmental inflammation are jointly associated with impaired sperm function in men with obstructive sleep apnea," the authors conclude.
paras.zh: “总而言之，这些发现支持了一个概念模型，其中睡眠呼吸障碍和局部精液微环境炎症与患有阻塞性睡眠呼吸暂停的男性精子功能受损共同相关，”作者总结道。

paras.en: The team is now calling for larger studies to "elucidate the precise molecular mechanisms and confirm the long-term fertility benefits of CPAP treatment."
paras.zh: 该团队现在呼吁进行更大规模的研究，以“阐明精确的分子机制并确认 CPAP 治疗的长期生育益处”。

paras.en: The research has been published in Sleep Medicine.
paras.zh: 该研究发表在《睡眠医学》杂志上。

articles.title: Belief in Magic Is Not Disappearing in The Modern World, Study Shows
articles.author: Esra Öz

paras.en: Imagine a house where footsteps supposedly echo through the hallways at night and doors close in empty rooms.
paras.zh: 想象一下，在一座房子里，夜晚的走廊里会回荡着脚步声，空荡荡的房间里门会关上。

paras.en: If you had to spend a night there, would explanations involving old floorboards and drafts be enough to settle your doubts?
paras.zh: 如果你必须在那里过夜，涉及旧地板和草稿的解释足以消除你的疑虑吗？

paras.en: As it happens, trusting a scientific explanation doesn't necessarily close the door on ghosts.
paras.zh: 碰巧的是，相信科学解释并不一定会关闭鬼魂的大门。

paras.en: A US study found that, among people who retained religious ties, an outlook combining support for science and reason with independence from religious authority was associated with stronger belief in magic, including ghosts and curses.
paras.zh: 美国的一项研究发现，在保留宗教联系的人中，将支持科学和理性与独立于宗教权威相结合的观点与对魔法（包括鬼魂和诅咒）的更强烈信仰有关。

paras.en: The researchers wanted to understand what happens to supernatural beliefs as religious institutions lose influence. When people question church teachings, do they also leave ghosts, curses, and unseen forces behind? Or do they begin choosing their beliefs for themselves?
paras.zh: 研究人员想了解当宗教机构失去影响力时，超自然信仰会发生什么。当人们质疑教会的教义时，他们是否也留下了鬼魂、诅咒和看不见的力量？或者他们开始​​为自己选择信仰？

paras.en: Sociologists Paul Froese of Baylor University and Isaiah King of Carson-Newman University, together with Ruiqian Li of American University, investigated these questions by analyzing survey responses from 1,812 adults in the 2025 Baylor Religion Survey.
paras.zh: 贝勒大学的社会学家 Paul Froese 和卡森纽曼大学的 Isaiah King 以及美利坚大学的 Ruiqian Li 通过分析 2025 年贝勒宗教调查中 1,812 名成年人的调查回复来调查这些问题。

paras.en: Gallup collected the answers online and by mail between January and March. Responses were weighted to better reflect the US adult population.
paras.zh: 盖洛普在一月至三月期间通过在线和邮寄方式收集了答案。对答复进行加权以更好地反映美国成年人口。

paras.en: The team examined an outlook they called "secular rationalism".
paras.zh: 该团队研究了一种他们称之为“世俗理性主义”的观点。

paras.en: This measure combines the view that science is the only way to understand all aspects of the world with an emphasis on reason and human experience in moral decisions, independent interpretation of spiritual teachings, and disinterest in religious discussions.
paras.zh: 这一措施结合了科学是理解世界各个方面的唯一途径的观点，强调道德决策中的理性和人类经验、对精神教义的独立解释以及对宗教讨论的不感兴趣。

paras.en: Scoring highly didn't necessarily mean cutting all religious ties. Some participants still believed in God, identified with a religion, or attended religious services.
paras.zh: 得分高并不一定意味着切断所有宗教联系。一些参与者仍然相信上帝、认同某种宗教或参加宗教仪式。

paras.en: The researchers compared these views with three categories of supernatural belief. They assessed miracles, magic, and everyday superstitions separately, distinguishing beliefs involving divine intervention from those that require no god or shared religious doctrine.
paras.zh: 研究人员将这些观点与三类超自然信仰进行了比较。他们分别评估奇迹、魔法和日常迷信，将涉及神圣干预的信仰与不需要上帝或共同宗教教义的信仰区分开来。

paras.en: Their magic score included belief in ghosts, curses, spirits inhabiting objects, communicating with the dead, predicting the future, and magic itself. Superstitions included habits such as avoiding words that might jinx a hoped-for outcome.
paras.zh: 他们的魔法分数包括相信鬼魂、诅咒、灵魂居住在物体上、与死者沟通、预测未来以及魔法本身。迷信包括避免使用可能给预期结果带来厄运的词语等习惯。

paras.en: The responses showed that people with higher secular rationalism scores were less likely to believe in miracles. Their scores for magic and superstition, however, were higher.
paras.zh: 调查结果显示，世俗理性主义得分较高的人不太可能相信奇迹。然而，他们在魔法和迷信方面的得分更高。

paras.en: Looking more closely, the researchers found that the association between secular rationalism and stronger magical belief appeared among people who kept these religious ties. The same association wasn't clearly evident among nonbelievers, people without a religious affiliation, and those who never attended services.
paras.zh: 更仔细地观察，研究人员发现，世俗理性主义和更强的魔法信仰之间的联系出现在保持这些宗教联系的人身上。在非信徒、没有宗教信仰的人和从不参加礼拜的人中，这种关联并不明显。

paras.en: In his account of the findings, Li described the differences among people who believed in God. Around 40 percent of those embracing secular rationalism leaned toward magical belief, compared with 19 percent of those rejecting that outlook.
paras.zh: 在对研究结果的描述中，李描述了信仰上帝的人之间的差异。大约 40% 的世俗理性主义拥护者倾向于魔法信仰，相比之下，19% 的人拒绝这种观点。

paras.en: The researchers' explanation centers on the distinction between personal faith and institutional authority. A religious community might accept miracles while rejecting fortune-telling or attempts to communicate with ghosts. A member who trusts their own judgment on spiritual matters might embrace those ideas anyway.
paras.zh: 研究人员的解释集中在个人信仰和机构权威之间的区别。宗教团体可能会接受奇迹，但拒绝算命或与鬼魂沟通的尝试。无论如何，一个相信自己对精神问题判断的成员可能会接受这些想法。

paras.en: This independence could allow supernatural beliefs to persist as trust in religious authority weakens. The survey responses are consistent with this possibility, although the survey didn't directly test how people developed their beliefs.
paras.zh: 当对宗教权威的信任减弱时，这种独立性可能会让超自然信仰继续存在。尽管调查没有直接测试人们如何形成自己的信念，但调查的答复与这种可能性是一致的。

paras.en: For sociologists, the findings suggest that questioning religious authority doesn't always mean abandoning supernatural beliefs.
paras.zh: 对于社会学家来说，研究结果表明质疑宗教权威并不总是意味着放弃超自然信仰。

paras.en: To understand what people believe, researchers may need to look beyond religious affiliation and consider how people combine faith, trust in science, and their own spiritual judgments. Two people attending the same church might have very different ideas about which unseen forces exist.
paras.zh: 为了了解人们的信仰，研究人员可能需要超越宗教信仰，并考虑人们如何将信仰、对科学的信任和他们自己的精神判断结合起来。参加同一教堂的两个人可能对存在哪些看不见的力量有截然不同的看法。

paras.en: The results don't establish that trusting science causes magical thinking. The rationalism measure wasn't a test of scientific knowledge or reasoning ability, either.
paras.zh: 结果并不能证明相信科学会引发神奇的思维。理性主义衡量标准也不是对科学知识或推理能力的测试。

paras.en: The survey also covered only US adults and captured their views during one period. It cannot reveal whether magical beliefs are becoming more or less common. Li noted that some comparison groups were small.
paras.zh: 这项调查还只涵盖了美国成年人，并捕捉了他们在某一时期的观点。它无法揭示魔法信仰是否变得越来越普遍或越来越不普遍。李指出，一些比较组很小。

paras.en: Following the same people over time could show how their supernatural beliefs change alongside their relationship with religion.
paras.zh: 随着时间的推移跟踪同一个人可以显示他们的超自然信仰如何随着他们与宗教的关系而变化。

paras.en: The house we imagined offers no evidence for ghosts. The study explores the beliefs someone might bring through its door: confidence in scientific explanations can still leave room for the possibility of an unseen presence.
paras.zh: 我们想象中的房子没有提供任何鬼魂存在的证据。这项研究探讨了人们可能会带来的信念：对科学解释的信心仍然可以为看不见的存在的可能性留下空间。

paras.en: The research has been published in Social Forces.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《社会力量》杂志上。

articles.title: Scientists discover Europe's ancient forests were nothing like we imagined

paras.en: Scientists discover Europe's ancient forests were nothing like we imagined
paras.zh: 科学家发现欧洲古老森林与我们想象的完全不同

paras.en: A sweeping 20-million-year study reveals that Europe's natural landscape was far more open and colorful than previously believed, raising troubling questions about today's massive tree-planting efforts.
paras.zh: 一项长达 2000 万年的全面研究表明，欧洲的自然景观远比之前想象的更加开放和丰富多彩，这对当今大规模的植树活动提出了令人不安的问题。

paras.en: - Scientists have uncovered evidence that Europe was dominated for more than 20 million years by open woodlands, colorful meadows, and large grazing animals, not the dense forests long considered its natural state. The surprising discovery challenges modern reforestation strategies, suggesting that planting thick forests could actually harm the biodiversity conservationists hope to protect.
paras.zh: - 科学家发现的证据表明，欧洲在超过 2000 万年的时间里一直被开阔的林地、色彩缤纷的草地和大型食草动物所统治，而不是长期以来被认为是其自然状态的茂密森林。这一令人惊讶的发现挑战了现代的重新造林策略，表明种植茂密的森林实际上可能会损害自然资源保护主义者希望保护的生物多样性。

paras.en: Picture the wilderness of central Europe 100,000 years ago, or even a million years ago. You might imagine an endless expanse of towering trees, with thick canopies blocking sunlight from reaching the ground. But according to a major new study, that familiar image of Europe's ancient forests is probably misleading.
paras.zh: 想象一下十万年前、甚至一百万年前中欧的荒野。你可能会想象一望无际的高耸树木，厚厚的树冠阻挡阳光到达地面。但根据一项重要的新研究，欧洲古老森林的熟悉形象可能具有误导性。

paras.en: Instead, much of the continent was a vibrant landscape of scattered trees, open woodlands, grassy clearings, and colorful wildflower meadows. Birds and butterflies flourished in these sunlit habitats, while enormous grazing animals helped prevent trees and shrubs from taking over.
paras.zh: 相反，这片大陆的大部分地区都是一片生机勃勃的风景，有稀疏的树木、开阔的林地、绿草如茵的空地和色彩缤纷的野花草地。鸟类和蝴蝶在这些阳光明媚的栖息地繁衍生息，而巨大的食草动物则有助于阻止树木和灌木的入侵。

paras.en: Researchers led by Aarhus University have found that this mixture of habitats dominated Europe's landscapes for more than 20 million years. Far from being the continent's original natural condition, the dense, dark forests common in many parts of Europe today appear to be a relatively recent development in its ecological history.
paras.zh: 奥尔胡斯大学领导的研究人员发现，这种混合栖息地在欧洲景观中占据主导地位超过 2000 万年。如今，欧洲许多地区常见的茂密、黑暗的森林远非欧洲大陆最初的自然条件，而是其生态历史上相对较新的发展。

paras.en: Published in Biological Conservation, the findings challenge a longstanding assumption about what Europe's wilderness looked like before widespread human intervention. They also raise important questions about modern reforestation programs, which often prioritize planting dense forests to combat climate change and protect biodiversity.
paras.zh: 该研究结果发表在《生物保护》杂志上，挑战了长期以来关于人类广泛干预之前欧洲荒野是什么样子的假设。他们还对现代重新造林计划提出了重要问题，这些计划通常优先考虑种植茂密的森林，以应对气候变化和保护生物多样性。

paras.en: "The study shows that current reforestation practices are on the wrong track - both here in Denmark, where subsidies are only granted for planting dense forests, and elsewhere in Europe. This will not only be harmful for biodiversity; it will be in direct contradiction to the type of ecosystems that Europe's species have evolved in over millions of years," says Professor Jens-Christian Svenning from the Center for Ecological Dynamics in a Novel Biosphere (ECONOVO), Department of Biology at Aarhus University, senior author of the study.
paras.zh: 奥尔胡斯大学生物系新型生物圈生态动力学中心（ECONOVO）的詹斯-克里斯蒂安·斯文宁（Jens-Christian Svenning）教授说：“这项研究表明，目前的重新造林做法走上了错误的道路——无论是在只为种植茂密森林提供补贴的丹麦，还是在欧洲其他地方。这不仅对生物多样性有害，而且与欧洲物种数百万年来进化的生态系统类型直接矛盾。”研究。

paras.en: Challenging the Myth of Europe's Ancient Forests
paras.zh: 挑战欧洲古老森林的神话

paras.en: For decades, conservation strategies have been influenced by the "closed-forest paradigm." This is the belief that dense forests with nearly continuous tree canopies were Europe's natural landscape before humans began clearing land for agriculture and settlements.
paras.zh: 几十年来，保护策略一直受到“封闭森林范式”的影响。人们相信，在人类开始清理土地用于农业和定居之前，拥有几乎连续的树冠的茂密森林是欧洲的自然景观。

paras.en: Under this view, restoring nature often means allowing trees to reclaim open areas or planting forests where they no longer exist.
paras.zh: 根据这种观点，恢复自然通常意味着允许树木开垦空地或在不再存在的地方种植森林。

paras.en: The new research suggests that this approach may overlook a crucial part of Europe's ecological history. Rather than being uniformly covered by dense forests, the continent was characterized by changing combinations of grasslands, shrubs, and woodlands with different amounts of tree cover.
paras.zh: 新的研究表明，这种方法可能忽视了欧洲生态历史的一个重要部分。这片大陆并不是均匀地被茂密的森林覆盖，而是草地、灌木和林地的组合不断变化，树木覆盖率也不同。

paras.en: These landscapes supported a rich variety of species adapted to both wooded and open environments. Large plant-eating animals also played a major role in maintaining this diversity by grazing, browsing, and disturbing vegetation.
paras.zh: 这些景观孕育了适应树木繁茂和开放环境的丰富物种。大型食草动物通过放牧、啃食和扰乱植被，在维持这种多样性方面也发挥了重要作用。

paras.en: What 23 Million Years of Evidence Reveals
paras.zh: 2300万年的证据揭示了什么

paras.en: To reconstruct Europe's ancient environments, the researchers examined an unusually extensive collection of evidence spanning millions of years.
paras.zh: 为了重建欧洲的古代环境，研究人员检查了跨越数百万年的异常广泛的证据收集。

paras.en: Previous studies have generally concentrated on more recent periods. This investigation extended much further into the past, examining paleoecological records from the Miocene epoch (which began around 23 million years ago) through the pre-industrial era.
paras.zh: 以前的研究通常集中在最近的时期。这项调查进一步延伸到了过去，考察了从中新世（大约开始于 2300 万年前）到前工业时代的古生态记录。

paras.en: Paleoecology is the study of ancient ecosystems using clues preserved in fossils, sediments, and other natural records. Because no single type of evidence can provide a complete picture of the distant past, the team combined several independent methods.
paras.zh: 古生态学是利用化石、沉积物和其他自然记录中保存的线索对古代生态系统进行研究。由于没有单一类型的证据可以提供遥远过去的完整画面，因此该团队结合了几种独立的方法。

paras.en: These included fossilized pollen and larger plant remains, charcoal left by ancient wildfires, and chemical signatures preserved in the teeth and bones of plant-eating animals. The researchers also examined fossil insects and mammals, along with ancient environmental DNA recovered from sediments.
paras.zh: 其中包括花粉化石和较大的植物遗骸、古代野火留下的木炭，以及食草动物牙齿和骨骼中保存的化学特征。研究人员还检查了昆虫和哺乳动物化石，以及从沉积物中回收的古代环境 DNA。

paras.en: Environmental DNA consists of genetic material left behind by organisms in their surroundings. When preserved in ancient deposits, it can help scientists identify plants and animals that lived in an area long ago.
paras.zh: 环境 DNA 由周围环境中的生物体留下的遗传物质组成。当它保存在古代沉积物中时，可以帮助科学家识别很久以前生活在某个地区的植物和动物。

paras.en: Together, these different sources of evidence allowed the researchers to reconstruct not only what types of vegetation existed, but also how ecosystems changed over time and how animals influenced their surroundings.
paras.zh: 总之，这些不同的证据来源使研究人员不仅可以重建存在的植被类型，还可以重建生态系统如何随时间变化以及动物如何影响周围环境。

paras.en: "Each type of proxy offers its own perspective, but together they let us see whether the landscapes were covered by dense forests, open grasslands, or a mix of the two. By combining these datasets across time - from the Miocene to the pre-industrial era - we could trace long-term changes in vegetation and the role of large herbivores with much greater confidence than earlier studies that used only one method," explains the study's lead author, ECONOVO PhD student Szymon Czyzewski of Aarhus University.
paras.zh: 该研究的主要作者、ECONOVO 博士生 Szymon Czyzewski 解释说：“每种类型的代理都提供了自己的视角，但它们一起让我们看到景观是否被茂密的森林、开阔的草原或两者的混合所覆盖。通过将这些不同时间的数据集（从中新世到前工业时代）结合起来，我们可以比仅使用一种方法的早期研究更有信心地追踪植被的长期变化和大型食草动物的作用。”奥胡斯大学。

paras.en: The evidence points to a consistent pattern. Across more than 20 million years, Europe's landscapes were typically a shifting mosaic of trees, open spaces, and flowering plants rather than continuous stretches of closed forest.
paras.zh: 证据表明存在一致的模式。在超过 2000 万年的时间里，欧洲的景观通常是由树木、开放空间和开花植物组成的不断变化的马赛克，而不是连续不断的封闭森林。

paras.en: Importantly, these mixed landscapes were not limited to one particular climate. They existed under temperate conditions comparable to those in much of Europe today, as well as during warmer and colder periods.
paras.zh: 重要的是，这些混合景观并不局限于一种特定的气候。它们存在于与当今欧洲大部分地区相当的温和条件下，以及温暖和寒冷的时期。

paras.en: Elephants, Rhinos, and Bison Shaped Europe's Wilderness
paras.zh: 大象、犀牛和野牛塑造了欧洲的荒野

paras.en: One of the most striking findings concerns the influence of large wild herbivores.
paras.zh: 最引人注目的发现之一涉及大型野生食草动物的影响。

paras.en: Ancient Europe was home to animals such as elephants, rhinoceroses, aurochs, and bison. By feeding on vegetation and disturbing the ground as they moved, these animals helped keep parts of the landscape open.
paras.zh: 古代欧洲是大象、犀牛、野牛和野牛等动物的家园。通过以植被为食并在移动时扰动地面，这些动物帮助保持了部分景观的开放。

paras.en: Their activities created opportunities for grasses, wildflowers, and other plants that might otherwise have struggled beneath dense tree cover.
paras.zh: 他们的活动为草、野花和其他植物创造了机会，否则这些植物可能会在茂密的树木覆盖下挣扎。

paras.en: This constant interaction between animals and vegetation helped sustain a diverse mixture of habitats, providing suitable conditions for many different species.
paras.zh: 动物和植被之间的这种持续相互作用有助于维持多样化的栖息地，为许多不同的物种提供合适的条件。

paras.en: Modern Europe, however, is missing much of this ecological influence. Many of the large wild herbivores that once shaped its landscapes have disappeared, and traditional grazing practices have also declined.
paras.zh: 然而，现代欧洲却忽视了这种生态影响。许多曾经塑造其景观的大型野生食草动物已经消失，传统的放牧方式也日渐式微。

paras.en: "The ecosystems we see in Europe today lack the large wild herbivores that not only shaped landscapes but also sustained its biodiversity for millions of years. The most dramatic shift has largely taken place within the last hundred years, when traditional extensive grazing disappeared from large parts of the landscape," says Czyzewski.
paras.zh: “我们今天在欧洲看到的生态系统缺乏大型野生食草动物，这些动物不仅塑造了景观，而且维持了数百万年的生物多样性。最戏剧性的变化主要发生在过去一百年里，当时传统的粗放放牧从大部分景观中消失了，”Czyzewski 说。

paras.en: This loss of grazing pressure has changed how vegetation develops across much of the continent, helping explain why present-day European ecosystems differ so dramatically from those of the distant past.
paras.zh: 放牧压力的丧失改变了非洲大陆大部分地区植被的发育方式，这有助于解释为什么当今欧洲的生态系统与遥远的过去有如此巨大的差异。

paras.en: Europe's Ancient Woodlands Were Full of Wildflowers
paras.zh: 欧洲古老的林地开满野花

paras.en: The research also offers a different perspective on species commonly associated with farmland and other human-managed environments.
paras.zh: 该研究还为通常与农田和其他人类管理环境相关的物种提供了不同的视角。

paras.en: Birds such as larks and jackdaws, along with mammals such as the European hamster, are often regarded as characteristic of agricultural landscapes. Yet the researchers suggest that their evolutionary histories likely extend back to the open woodland environments that existed long before modern farming.
paras.zh: 云雀和寒鸦等鸟类以及欧洲仓鼠等哺乳动物通常被视为农业景观的特征。然而研究人员认为，它们的进化历史很可能可以追溯到现代农业出现之前很久就存在的开阔林地环境。

paras.en: Even familiar wildflowers have connections to these ancient ecosystems.
paras.zh: 即使是熟悉的野花也与这些古老的生态系统有联系。

paras.en: Wild poppies, now frequently seen growing in agricultural fields, also thrived in areas where large grazing animals disturbed vegetation within ancient woodlands.
paras.zh: 野生罂粟现在常见于农田中，在大型食草动物扰乱古代林地植被的地区也蓬勃发展。

paras.en: These findings challenge the sharp distinction between "forest" and "open habitats" that often guides conservation planning today.
paras.zh: 这些发现挑战了当今经常指导保护规划的“森林”和“开放栖息地”之间的鲜明区别。

paras.en: In Europe's ecological past, trees, meadows, shrubs, and grazing animals were not necessarily separate parts of nature. They frequently existed together, forming interconnected habitats that supported a wide range of wildlife.
paras.zh: 在欧洲的生态历史中，树木、草地、灌木和食草动物不一定是自然的独立部分。它们经常一起存在，形成相互关联的栖息地，支持各种野生动物。

paras.en: Why Planting More Trees May Not Always Help Nature
paras.zh: 为什么种植更多的树木并不总能帮助大自然

paras.en: The findings arrive as European countries continue expanding forests to capture carbon dioxide, address climate change, and restore biodiversity.
paras.zh: 这一发现是在欧洲国家继续扩大森林以捕获二氧化碳、应对气候变化和恢复生物多样性之际得出的。

paras.en: Although forests can provide important environmental benefits, the researchers argue that planting large areas of uniformly dense woodland may not be the best approach when the goal is to restore Europe's native ecosystems.
paras.zh: 尽管森林可以提供重要的环境效益，但研究人员认为，当目标是恢复欧洲本土生态系统时，种植大面积均匀密集的林地可能不是最好的方法。

paras.en: Many European species evolved in landscapes containing a mixture of trees and open areas. Converting these habitats into continuous closed-canopy forests could therefore reduce the variety of environments available to wildlife.
paras.zh: 许多欧洲物种是在树木和开阔区域混合的景观中进化而来的。因此，将这些栖息地转变为连续的封闭林冠森林可能会减少野生动物可利用的环境多样性。

paras.en: The study suggests that restoration efforts should focus more strongly on maintaining diverse landscapes, including open grasslands, scattered woodland, and areas shaped by natural grazing.
paras.zh: 研究表明，恢复工作应更加注重维护多样化的景观，包括开阔的草原、分散的林地和自然放牧形成的区域。

paras.en: "Instead, restoration efforts should place greater emphasis on creating and maintaining mosaics of woodland and open habitats - not least through the restoration of natural-living large herbivores," Svenning concludes.
paras.zh: 斯文宁总结道：“相反，恢复工作应该更加重视创造和维护林地和开放栖息地的马赛克，尤其是通过恢复自然生活的大型食草动物。”

paras.en: The findings add to a growing body of research from the same scientific group suggesting that large animals played a far greater role in shaping Europe's ecosystems than previously recognized.
paras.zh: 同一科学小组越来越多的研究结果表明，大型动物在塑造欧洲生态系统方面发挥的作用比以前认识到的要大得多。

paras.en: They also reinforce the idea that Europe's ancient landscapes were generally brighter, more open, and more varied than the dense primeval forests often depicted in popular imagination.
paras.zh: 它们还强化了这样一种观念，即欧洲古代景观通常比大众想象中茂密的原始森林更明亮、更开放、更多样化。

paras.en: Rather than restoring nature by simply planting more trees, the researchers suggest that protecting biodiversity may require recreating the complex balance of woodlands, meadows, and grazing animals that shaped the continent for millions of years.
paras.zh: 研究人员认为，保护生物多样性可能需要重建数百万年来塑造这片大陆的林地、草地和食草动物之间的复杂平衡，而不是简单地种植更多树木来恢复自然。

paras.en: The familiar image of Europe as a vast, dark, unbroken forest may be deeply rooted in our understanding of nature, but millions of years of evidence are painting a very different picture.
paras.zh: 欧洲作为一片广阔、黑暗、连绵不断的森林的熟悉形象可能深深植根于我们对自然的理解中，但数百万年的证据正在描绘一幅截然不同的画面。

paras.en: Materials provided by Aarhus University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由奥胡斯大学提供。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。

articles.title: Human bodies produce 2 billion metric tons of CO2 a year just by staying alive

paras.en: Human bodies produce 2 billion metric tons of CO2 a year just by staying alive
paras.zh: 人体仅靠生存每年就会产生 20 亿吨二氧化碳

paras.en: - Humans collectively produce more than 2 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide annually just by turning food into energy, a 74% increase over three decades largely driven by population growth. Unlike fossil fuel emissions, however, the CO2 we exhale is part of the natural carbon cycle, and scientists say measuring it more accurately could improve climate models.
paras.zh: - 人类仅通过将食物转化为能源，每年就总共产生超过 20 亿吨二氧化碳，这在 30 年来增加了 74%，这主要是由人口增长推动的。然而，与化石燃料排放不同的是，我们呼出的二氧化碳是自然碳循环的一部分，科学家表示，更准确地测量它可以改善气候模型。

paras.en: Every human body produces carbon dioxide simply by converting food into energy. Although the amount released by one person may seem small, the combined output of billions of people adds up to an enormous quantity.
paras.zh: 每个人体只需将食物转化为能量就会产生二氧化碳。虽然一个人释放的量看起来很小，但数十亿人释放的总量加起来就是一个巨大的量。

paras.en: A new study led by the University of Bath estimates that carbon dioxide production from human metabolism increased by 74% between 1985 and 2015, reaching 2.05 billion metric tons annually. The researchers found that the dramatic rise was primarily the result of population growth, rather than a substantial increase in how much CO2 each person produces.
paras.zh: 巴斯大学领导的一项新研究估计，1985 年至 2015 年间，人类新陈代谢产生的二氧化碳增加了 74%，每年达到 20.5 亿吨。研究人员发现，这种急剧上升主要是人口增长的结果，而不是每个人产生的二氧化碳量大幅增加的结果。

paras.en: The findings could help scientists better understand the global carbon cycle, which describes how carbon moves between the atmosphere, living organisms, oceans, and land. By measuring humanity's contribution more accurately, researchers hope to improve predictions about how well efforts to reduce carbon emissions will work.
paras.zh: 这些发现可以帮助科学家更好地了解全球碳循环，它描述了碳如何在大气、生物体、海洋和陆地之间移动。通过更准确地衡量人类的贡献，研究人员希望改进对减少碳排放的努力效果的预测。

paras.en: Why Human CO2 Emissions Are Different From Fossil Fuels
paras.zh: 为什么人类二氧化碳排放量与化石燃料排放量不同

paras.en: Despite the enormous numbers, the researchers emphasize that the carbon dioxide produced by human metabolism is fundamentally different from the emissions generated by burning fossil fuels.
paras.zh: 尽管数量巨大，但研究人员强调，人类新陈代谢产生的二氧化碳与燃烧化石燃料产生的排放有着根本的不同。

paras.en: When people breathe out CO2, most of that carbon originally came from the food they consumed. Plants absorbed it from the atmosphere relatively recently, meaning it is already circulating through the natural carbon cycle.
paras.zh: 当人们呼出二氧化碳时，大部分碳最初来自他们消耗的食物。植物最近从大气中吸收了它，这意味着它已经通过自然碳循环循环。

paras.en: Burning coal, oil, and natural gas is different. These fuels contain carbon that has remained trapped underground for millions of years. Burning them releases that long-stored carbon into the atmosphere, adding to the amount of CO2 circulating through the Earth's climate system.
paras.zh: 燃烧煤炭、石油和天然气是不同的。这些燃料含有碳，这些碳已被困在地下数百万年。燃烧它们会将长期储存的碳释放到大气中，增加了地球气候系统中循环的二氧化碳量。

paras.en: The new research, published in The Lancet Planetary Health, was led by Professor Javier Gonzalez of the University of Bath's Centre for Exercise, Nutrition and Metabolism.
paras.zh: 这项新研究发表在《柳叶刀行星健康》上，由巴斯大学运动、营养和代谢中心的哈维尔·冈萨雷斯教授领导。

paras.en: The team calculated that global CO2 production from human metabolism climbed from 1.18 billion metric tons in 1985 to 2.05 billion metric tons in 2015. More than 60% of that increase could be attributed to the growing number of people worldwide.
paras.zh: 研究小组计算出，全球人类新陈代谢产生的二氧化碳从1985年的11.8亿吨攀升至2015年的20.5亿吨。其中60%以上的增长可归因于全世界人口数量的增长。

paras.en: "We all produce carbon dioxide simply by turning food into energy, but until now we haven't had a good idea how much that adds up to worldwide.
paras.zh: “我们只是通过将食物转化为能源来产生二氧化碳，但直到现在我们还不清楚全世界总共产生了多少二氧化碳。

paras.en: "What we've found is that the increase is mainly because there are more of us. This gives scientists one more piece of the puzzle when working out where carbon comes from and where it goes. Ultimately, this information can help scientists more accurately predict how effective carbon reduction strategies may be."
paras.zh: “我们发现，这种增加主要是因为我们的人数增加了。这为科学家们在弄清楚碳从何而来和去往何处时提供了又一个难题。最终，这些信息可以帮助科学家更准确地预测碳减排策略的有效性。”

paras.en: How Scientists Measured Humanity's CO2 Production
paras.zh: 科学家如何测量人类的二氧化碳排放量

paras.en: To estimate how much carbon dioxide people generate, the researchers analyzed thousands of measurements collected from individuals across the human lifespan, from infants to older adults.
paras.zh: 为了估计人们产生的二氧化碳量，研究人员分析了从婴儿到老年人的整个人类生命周期中收集的数千个测量数据。

paras.en: These measurements provided information about the CO2 produced by the body during ordinary daily activities. The team then combined those findings with worldwide population figures and body weight data to calculate how human metabolic CO2 production had changed over time.
paras.zh: 这些测量提供了有关身体在日常活动中产生的二氧化碳的信息。然后，研究小组将这些发现与全球人口数据和体重数据相结合，计算出人类代谢二氧化碳产生量随时间的变化。

paras.en: The results showed that population growth was the dominant factor behind the 74% increase. Changes in the amount of carbon dioxide generated by individual people played a much smaller role.
paras.zh: 结果显示，人口增长是74%增长背后的主导因素。个人产生的二氧化碳量的变化所起的作用要小得多。

paras.en: Accurately measuring this process is important because human metabolism contributes to the continuous movement of carbon through the environment. Its influence on local carbon measurements can be especially noticeable in densely populated cities and urban areas, where large numbers of people live and work close together.
paras.zh: 准确测量这一过程非常重要，因为人体新陈代谢有助于碳在环境中的持续移动。它对当地碳测量的影响在人口稠密的城市和城市地区尤其明显，那里有大量的人生活和工作在一起。

paras.en: Understanding these contributions can help researchers develop more complete carbon budgets, which track the sources, movements, and destinations of carbon within the Earth's systems.
paras.zh: 了解这些贡献可以帮助研究人员制定更完整的碳预算，跟踪地球系统内碳的来源、移动和目的地。

paras.en: Scientists Stress That Breathing Is Not Driving Climate Change
paras.zh: 科学家强调呼吸并不是导致气候变化的原因

paras.en: Although the study reveals a surprisingly large amount of CO2 production, its findings should not be interpreted as evidence that human breathing is a major cause of global warming.
paras.zh: 尽管该研究揭示了二氧化碳的产生量惊人，但其发现不应被解释为人类呼吸是全球变暖的主要原因的证据。

paras.en: The researchers are not recommending that people reduce their physical activity or change their diets to lower the carbon dioxide produced by their bodies. Instead, the goal is to make scientific measurements and calculations of the global carbon cycle more accurate.
paras.zh: 研究人员并不建议人们减少体力活动或改变饮食来降低身体产生的二氧化碳。相反，目标是使全球碳循环的科学测量和计算更加准确。

paras.en: Distinguishing between carbon dioxide produced through natural biological processes and carbon released by burning fossil fuels is essential for understanding the planet's changing climate.
paras.zh: 区分自然生物过程产生的二氧化碳和燃烧化石燃料释放的碳对于了解地球气候变化至关重要。

paras.en: Professor Gonzalez emphasized this distinction:
paras.zh: 冈萨雷斯教授强调了这一区别：

paras.en: "The important thing is that the carbon dioxide we breathe out is not the same as burning fossil fuels. We're not saying that breathing is driving climate change.
paras.zh: “重要的是，我们呼出的二氧化碳与燃烧化石燃料不同。我们并不是说呼吸正在推动气候变化。

paras.en: "What this study does is give us a much clearer picture of how much CO2 people produce around the world, and how that is changing as the population grows. This understanding can help improve the accuracy predictions of carbon reduction programs."
paras.zh: “这项研究的目的是让我们更清楚地了解世界各地人们产生了多少二氧化碳，以及随着人口增长而发生的变化。这种了解可以帮助提高碳减排计划的准确性预测。”

paras.en: By establishing a clearer picture of humanity's metabolic CO2 production, the researchers have provided another piece of information scientists can use to track global carbon movements and evaluate strategies for reducing emissions.
paras.zh: 通过更清晰地了解人类代谢二氧化碳的产生，研究人员提供了另一条信息，科学家可以用它来跟踪全球碳运动并评估减少排放的策略。

paras.en: Funding: The IAEA doubly labeled water database was financially supported by the International Atomic Energy Agency, Taiyo Nippon Sanso, and SERCON.
paras.zh: 资助：国际原子能机构双重标记水数据库得到国际原子能机构、大阳日酸和 SERCON 的财政支持。

articles.title: Drinking 2–3 cups of coffee a day linked to dramatically lower dementia risk

paras.en: Drinking 2â3 cups of coffee a day linked to dramatically lower dementia risk
paras.zh: 每天喝 2â3 杯咖啡可显着降低痴呆风险

paras.en: - Drinking two to three cups of caffeinated coffee daily was linked to a dramatically lower risk of dementia and better cognitive functioning in a study spanning up to 43 years. The benefits appeared regardless of genetic risk, but decaffeinated coffee did not show the same association.
paras.zh: - 一项长达 43 年的研究显示，每天喝两到三杯含咖啡因的咖啡可以显着降低患痴呆症的风险，并改善认知功能。无论遗传风险如何，这些好处都会出现，但不含咖啡因的咖啡并没有表现出同样的关联。

paras.en: Your daily cup of coffee may be doing more than helping you wake up in the morning. A long-running study of U.S. adults suggests that drinking caffeinated coffee regularly is associated with a substantially lower risk of dementia and better cognitive health as people age.
paras.zh: 您每天喝一杯咖啡的作用可能不仅仅是帮助您早上醒来。一项针对美国成年人的长期研究表明，随着人们年龄的增长，经常喝含咖啡因的咖啡可以显着降低患痴呆症的风险，并改善认知健康。

paras.en: Researchers found that adults who consumed higher amounts of caffeinated coffee developed dementia at considerably lower rates than those who rarely or never drank it. The findings were based on follow-up periods extending as long as 43 years, offering a valuable look at how everyday drinking habits relate to brain health over time.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，饮用大量含咖啡因咖啡的成年人患痴呆症的几率比很少或从不喝咖啡的人要低得多。该研究结果基于长达 43 年的随访期，为了解日常饮酒习惯与大脑健康之间的关系提供了有价值的视角。

paras.en: The strongest associations appeared among people who drank two to three cups of caffeinated coffee each day. Tea consumption was also linked to better cognitive outcomes, although the amount associated with the greatest benefit was somewhat lower.
paras.zh: 每天喝两到三杯含咖啡因咖啡的人之间的关联最为强烈。喝茶也与更好的认知结果有关，尽管与最大益处相关的量略低。

paras.en: Interestingly, decaffeinated coffee did not show the same benefits, raising questions about whether caffeine itself might help explain the connection.
paras.zh: 有趣的是，不含咖啡因的咖啡并没有表现出同样的好处，这引发了人们对咖啡因本身是否有助于解释这种联系的疑问。

paras.en: Coffee Drinkers Showed Much Lower Dementia Rates
paras.zh: 喝咖啡的人痴呆症发病率要低得多

paras.en: One of the most striking findings involved the difference in dementia rates between regular coffee drinkers and people who consumed little or no coffee.
paras.zh: 最引人注目的发现之一是经常喝咖啡的人和很少喝咖啡或不喝咖啡的人之间的痴呆症发病率存在差异。

paras.en: Among U.S. adults who drank higher amounts of caffeinated coffee, researchers recorded 141 dementia cases annually for every 100,000 people. In comparison, the rate was 330 cases per 100,000 people each year among those who rarely or never drank caffeinated coffee.
paras.zh: 研究人员记录，在饮用较多含咖啡因咖啡的美国成年人中，每年每 10 万人中有 141 例患有痴呆症。相比之下，在那些很少或从不喝含咖啡因咖啡的人中，每年每 10 万人中有 330 例患病。

paras.en: Dementia is a general term for conditions that progressively interfere with memory, thinking, reasoning, and the ability to perform everyday activities. Alzheimer's disease is its most common cause, although several other brain disorders can also lead to dementia.
paras.zh: 痴呆症是逐渐干扰记忆、思维、推理和日常活动能力的疾病的总称。阿尔茨海默氏病是其最常见的原因，尽管其他几种脑部疾病也可能导致痴呆症。

paras.en: While occasional forgetfulness can be a normal part of aging, dementia involves cognitive difficulties severe enough to disrupt daily life. Identifying lifestyle habits associated with lower dementia risk is therefore an important area of research, particularly as populations grow older.
paras.zh: 虽然偶尔健忘可能是衰老的正常现象，但痴呆症会导致认知困难，严重程度足以扰乱日常生活。因此，识别与降低痴呆风险相关的生活习惯是一个重要的研究领域，特别是随着人口老龄化。

paras.en: The findings suggest that regular caffeinated coffee consumption may be one such habit. However, the results show an association rather than proving that coffee directly prevents dementia. Other differences between coffee drinkers and people who avoid coffee could also contribute to the observed results.
paras.zh: 研究结果表明，经常饮用含咖啡因的咖啡可能就是这样的习惯之一。然而，结果显示了一种关联，而不是证明咖啡可以直接预防痴呆症。喝咖啡的人和不喝咖啡的人之间的其他差异也可能导致观察到的结果。

paras.en: Coffee Was Also Linked to Better Cognitive Health
paras.zh: 咖啡也与更好的认知健康有关

paras.en: The potential benefits were not limited to diagnosed dementia. Participants who drank more caffeinated coffee were also less likely to report that their memory or thinking abilities had declined.
paras.zh: 潜在的好处不仅限于诊断出的痴呆症。喝更多含咖啡因咖啡的参与者也不太可能报告他们的记忆或思维能力下降。

paras.en: Researchers found that 7.8% of adults who consumed higher amounts of caffeinated coffee reported subjective cognitive decline, compared with 9.5% of those who rarely or never drank it.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，饮用大量含咖啡因咖啡的成年人中，有 7.8% 的人主观认知能力下降，而很少或从不喝咖啡的成年人中，这一比例为 9.5%。

paras.en: Subjective cognitive decline refers to changes in memory or thinking that people notice themselves, even when those difficulties have not necessarily been confirmed by formal cognitive testing. Someone experiencing it might feel that remembering information, concentrating, or finding the right words has become more difficult.
paras.zh: 主观认知衰退是指人们注意到自己的记忆或思维发生变化，即使这些困难不一定通过正式的认知测试得到证实。经历过这种情况的人可能会觉得记住信息、集中注意力或找到正确的词语变得更加困难。

paras.en: Such complaints do not automatically indicate dementia. Nevertheless, they can provide useful information about how people perceive changes in their cognitive abilities as they grow older.
paras.zh: 此类投诉并不自动表明患有痴呆症。尽管如此，它们可以提供有用的信息，说明人们如何看待随着年龄的增长认知能力的变化。

paras.en: The lower percentage among caffeinated coffee drinkers adds to the evidence linking coffee consumption with healthier cognitive aging.
paras.zh: 喝咖啡因的人比例较低，这进一步证明了咖啡消费与更健康的认知衰老之间的联系。

paras.en: How Much Coffee Offers the Greatest Benefit?
paras.zh: 喝多少咖啡能带来最大的好处？

paras.en: The researchers also examined whether the amount of coffee consumed was related to the strength of the observed benefits.
paras.zh: 研究人员还研究了咖啡的摄入量是否与观察到的益处的强度有关。

paras.en: Drinking two to three cups of caffeinated coffee per day was associated with the most favorable outcomes for dementia risk and cognitive functioning.
paras.zh: 每天喝两到三杯含咖啡因的咖啡与痴呆风险和认知功能的最有利结果相关。

paras.en: Notably, this association remained apparent regardless of participants' genetic risk of developing dementia. In other words, the relationship between coffee consumption and brain health was observed even among people whose inherited characteristics might make them more vulnerable to the disease.
paras.zh: 值得注意的是，无论参与者患痴呆症的遗传风险如何，这种关联仍然很明显。换句话说，即使在遗传特征可能使他们更容易患这种疾病的人中，也观察到了咖啡摄入量与大脑健康之间的关系。

paras.en: Genetic risk refers to the influence of inherited variations in DNA that can increase or decrease a person's likelihood of developing certain conditions. Although genetics can play an important role in dementia, they are only one part of a much larger picture that includes age, general health, and lifestyle.
paras.zh: 遗传风险是指 DNA 遗传变异的影响，它会增加或减少一个人患某些疾病的可能性。尽管遗传学在痴呆症中发挥着重要作用，但它们只是包括年龄、总体健康状况和生活方式在内的更大图景的一部分。

paras.en: The results also suggest that drinking larger amounts of coffee is not necessarily better. Consumption beyond the range associated with the strongest benefits did not appear to provide additional protection.
paras.zh: 研究结果还表明，喝更多的咖啡并不一定就更好。超出与最强益处相关的范围的消费似乎并没有提供额外的保护。

paras.en: Tea Drinkers May Benefit Too, but Decaf Was Different
paras.zh: 喝茶的人也可能受益，但脱咖啡因则不同

paras.en: Coffee was not the only beverage associated with better brain health. Researchers found that drinking tea was also linked to lower dementia risk and better cognitive functioning.
paras.zh: 咖啡并不是唯一与改善大脑健康相关的饮料。研究人员发现，喝茶还可以降低痴呆风险和改善认知功能。

paras.en: For tea, the strongest associations appeared among participants who consumed one to two cups per day. As with coffee, drinking more than this amount did not appear to produce further benefits.
paras.zh: 对于茶，最强烈的关联出现在每天喝一到两杯茶的参与者中。与咖啡一样，喝超过这个量似乎不会产生进一步的好处。

paras.en: However, the study did not distinguish between caffeinated and noncaffeinated tea. As a result, the findings cannot establish whether caffeine was responsible for the association observed among tea drinkers.
paras.zh: 然而，该研究没有区分含咖啡因的茶和不含咖啡因的茶。因此，研究结果无法确定咖啡因是否与饮茶者之间观察到的关联有关。

paras.en: The results for coffee offered an additional clue. While regular caffeinated coffee was associated with lower dementia risk and better cognitive outcomes, decaffeinated coffee did not demonstrate the same benefits.
paras.zh: 咖啡的结果提供了额外的线索。虽然普通的含咖啡因咖啡与较低的痴呆风险和更好的认知结果相关，但不含咖啡因的咖啡并没有表现出相同的好处。

paras.en: Caffeine is a naturally occurring stimulant found in coffee, tea, and several other plants. It acts on the central nervous system and is best known for temporarily increasing alertness and reducing feelings of tiredness.
paras.zh: 咖啡因是一种天然存在的兴奋剂，存在于咖啡、茶和其他几种植物中。它作用于中枢神经系统，以暂时提高警觉性和减少疲劳感而闻名。

paras.en: Whether caffeine also contributes to better brain health over many years is a separate question. The difference between regular and decaffeinated coffee makes this possibility worth investigating, but it does not establish caffeine as the cause of the observed benefits.
paras.zh: 多年来咖啡因是否也有助于改善大脑健康是一个单独的问题。普通咖啡和脱咖啡因咖啡之间的差异使得这种可能性值得研究，但它并没有将咖啡因确定为观察到的益处的原因。

paras.en: Taken together, the findings suggest that moderate consumption of caffeinated coffee and tea may be associated with healthier brain aging. For coffee drinkers, two to three cups daily appeared to offer the strongest association, while one to two cups of tea showed the most favorable results among tea drinkers.
paras.zh: 综上所述，研究结果表明，适量饮用含咖啡因的咖啡和茶可能与更健康的大脑衰老有关。对于咖啡饮用者来说，每天喝两到三杯似乎提供了最强的关联，而对于喝茶的人来说，每天喝一到两杯茶显示出最有利的结果。

paras.en: Although additional research is needed to determine whether these beverages directly influence dementia risk, the long-term findings offer encouraging news for people who already enjoy coffee or tea as part of their daily routine.
paras.zh: 尽管还需要进行更多研究来确定这些饮料是否直接影响痴呆症风险，但长期研究结果为那些已经将咖啡或茶作为日常生活一部分的人们提供了令人鼓舞的消息。

articles.title: Send your name to Saturn's moon Titan with NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission
articles.author: Elizabeth Howell

paras.en: We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission.
paras.zh: 我们距离将人类送往太阳系遥远的地方可能还需要一段时间，但你可以将你的名字发送到土星的卫星泰坦，由于美国宇航局的蜻蜓任务，泰坦表面拥有生命成分。

paras.en: Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027.
paras.zh: “蜻蜓”是一种 SUV 大小的核动力旋翼机，NASA 计划于 2028 年向土卫六发射。该机构于 10 月下旬开设了一个特别活动页面，允许公众在飞船上留下自己的名字。这些名字将在飞船组装期间被记录在蜻蜓号的芯片上，所有名字必须在 2027 年 1 月 15 日之前提交。

paras.en: The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034. "Nearly a billion miles away, an extraordinary destination awaits. Titan has an atmosphere, rivers and lakes, seasons, sweeping dunes and a landscape rich in organic material," NASA officials wrote in the event page. "Upon arrival in 2034, Dragonfly will fly from place to place on this intriguing world to uncover clues about this remarkable moon, and the chemistry that could help us understand the ingredients for life."
paras.zh: 该机构表示，这次任务没有“普通的行程”，因为“蜻蜓”号的目标是在 2034 年抵达地表后相距数英里（或公里）的地区。“在近十亿英里之外，一个非凡的目的地正在等待着。土卫六有大气层、河流和湖泊、季节、广阔的沙丘和富含有机物质的景观，”美国宇航局官员在活动页面中写道。 “2034 年抵达后，‘蜻蜓’号将在这个迷人的世界中从一个地方飞到另一个地方，以发现有关这颗非凡卫星的线索，以及可以帮助我们了解生命成分的化学物质。”

paras.en: Dragonfly will be one of just a few flying crafts on another world, with the first being NASA's plucky Ingenuity mini-helicopter that arrived on Mars along with the still-running Perseverance rover in 2021. Ingenuity was only designed to make five flights, but made it to 72 until its blades were damaged during a landing on Jan. 18, 2024.
paras.zh: 蜻蜓号将是前往另一个世界的少数飞行器之一，第一架是 NASA 勇敢的 Ingenuity 迷你直升机，它与仍在运行的毅力号火星车一起于 2021 年抵达火星。Ingenuity 原本只设计进行 5 次飞行，但它的飞行次数达到了 72 次，直到 2024 年 1 月 18 日着陆时叶片受损。

paras.en: NASA is now planning a SkyFall mission on Mars that would use three helicopters, and which may launch as soon as late 2028 for the Red Planet.
paras.zh: NASA 目前正在计划在火星上执行 SkyFall 任务，该任务将使用三架直升机，最早可能于 2028 年年底在这颗红色星球上发射。

paras.en: Dragonfly, however, is not the first mission to Titan: that would be Huygens, which operated for just a few hours on Jan. 14, 2005 after deploying from the Cassini spacecraft. Huygens was the first lander on an outer solar system world, and measured Titan's atmosphere and took data from the surface.
paras.zh: 然而，蜻蜓号并不是第一个前往土卫六的任务：惠更斯号在 2005 年 1 月 14 日从卡西尼号飞船部署后仅运行了几个小时。惠更斯号是太阳系外世界的第一个着陆器，测量了泰坦的大气层并从表面获取了数据。

paras.en: For its part, Cassini flew by Titan more than 100 times before the mission concluded in September 2017, providing valuable long-term data about the moon from above. Dragonfly aims to show the moon from up close for about 3.3 Earth years. Its destinations will include dunes and a young impact crater called Selk, according to NASA.
paras.zh: 就卡西尼号而言，在 2017 年 9 月任务结束之前，卡西尼号飞越泰坦超过 100 次，从上方提供了有关泰坦的宝贵长期数据。蜻蜓计划在约 3.3 个地球年的时间内近距离展示月球。据美国宇航局称，它的目的地将包括沙丘和一个名为塞尔克的年轻撞击坑。

paras.en: "Dragonfly is expected to make one flight every one to two Titan days, which is called a Tsol and lasts about 16 Earth days," NASA officials added of the mission. Dragonfly will stop at a variety of geologic sites, where it will collect samples of surface material for analysis inside the rotorcraft by a suite of scientific instruments."
paras.zh: NASA 官员在谈到此次任务时补充道：“蜻蜓预计每隔一到两个泰坦日进行一次飞行，这被称为 Tsol，持续约 16 个地球日。”蜻蜓号将在多个地质地点停留，收集地表物质样本，并通过一套科学仪器在旋翼机内进行分析。”

paras.en: Dragonfly's goals include learning more about prebiotic chemistry, or the conditions prior to life arising in a location; figuring out if Titan had habitable conditions in the past; and looking for "chemical indicators" of life based on water or hydrocarbons.
paras.zh: 蜻蜓的目标包括更多地了解生命起源之前的化学，或者某个地方生命出现之前的条件；弄清楚土卫六过去是否具有适宜居住的条件；并寻找基于水或碳氢化合物的生命“化学指标”。

paras.en: Elizabeth Howell (she/her), Ph.D., was a staff writer in the spaceflight channel between 2022 and 2024 specializing in Canadian space news. She was contributing writer for Space.com for 10 years from 2012 to 2024. Elizabeth's reporting includes multiple exclusives with the White House, leading world coverage about a lost-and-found space tomato on the International Space Station, witnessing five human spaceflight launches on two continents, flying parabolic, working inside a spacesuit, and participating in a simulated Mars mission. Her latest book, "Why Am I Taller?" (ECW Press, 2022) is co-written with astronaut Dave Williams.
paras.zh: 伊丽莎白·豪厄尔（Elizabeth Howell）（她/她）博士于 2022 年至 2024 年间担任太空飞行频道的特约撰稿人，专门报道加拿大太空新闻。从 2012 年到 2024 年，她在 Space.com 担任特约撰稿人长达 10 年。伊丽莎白的报道内容包括多份白宫独家报道、主导国际空间站失物招领太空番茄的全球报道、见证五次载人航天在两大洲的发射、抛物线飞行、在宇航服内工作以及参与模拟火星任务。她的最新书《为什么我更高？》 （ECW Press，2022 年）与宇航员戴夫·威廉姆斯 (Dave Williams) 共同撰写。

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
articles.author: Hanneke Weitering

paras.en: On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years!
paras.zh: 1996 年 11 月 7 日，美国宇航局启动了火星全球探测者任务。这是近 20 年来 NASA 首次执行火星任务！

paras.en: The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner, Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water.
paras.zh: 火星全球探测者号航天器是一个轨道飞行器。它将美国宇航局火星漫游者旅居者号、勇气号和机遇号的数据传输回地球。该航天器还做了很多自己的科学研究。它发现火星表面的通道似乎是由流水形成的。

paras.en: Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites.
paras.zh: 火星全球探测者号观察了火星南极，发现了可能发生气候变化的迹象。它还在火星上发现了一种叫做赤铁矿的矿物。赤铁矿通常在水中形成。美国宇航局随后派出勇气号和机遇号火星车去寻找赤铁矿，两辆火星车都在着陆点附近发现了它。

paras.en: Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected. But a space maneuver accidentally exposed one of its batteries to the sun, and the spacecraft lost power. It fell silent forever in November 2006.
paras.zh: 火星全球探测者号的存活时间比预期的要长得多。但一次太空机动意外地将其中一个电池暴露在阳光下，航天器失去了动力。 2006年11月，它永远沉寂了。

paras.en: As the first successful Mars mission since the two Viking launches in 1975, Mars Global Surveyor ushered in a new era of exploration of the Red Planet, not only through its own contributions to orbit-based science, but by serving a relay for surface-based rovers. As such, it became a primary pipeline for multiple concurrent Mars missions.
paras.zh: 作为自 1975 年两次维京号发射以来首次成功的火星任务，火星全球勘测者号不仅通过自身对轨道科学的贡献，而且通过为地面漫游车提供中继服务，开创了探索这颗红色星球的新时代。因此，它成为多个并发火星任务的主要管道。

paras.en: "The [Mars Global Surveyor] mission overhauled scientists' understanding of Mars by studying the entire Martian surface, atmosphere and interior. Major findings included dramatic evidence that water still flows on Mars in short bursts down hillside gullies, and the identification of water-related mineral deposits leading to selection of a Mars rover landing site for a subsequent mission," read a NASA description of the probe.
paras.zh: “火星全球探测者号任务通过研究整个火星表面、大气层和内部，彻底改变了科学家对火星的认识。主要发现包括明显的证据，表明火星上的水仍然在短时间内沿着山坡沟壑流淌，并且识别出与水有关的矿藏，从而为后续任务选择了火星车着陆点，”美国宇航局对该探测器的描述中写道。

paras.en: Mars Global Surveyor sent back more than 240,000 images to Earth during its nine active years.
paras.zh: 火星全球探测者号在其活跃的九年里向地球发回了超过 24 万张图像。

paras.en: Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube.
paras.zh: 想要更多太空历史吗？查看我们完整的“太空中的这一天”故事存档，并在 YouTube 上观看“太空中的这一天”视频。

paras.en: Hanneke Weitering is a multimedia journalist in the Pacific Northwest reporting on the future of aviation at FutureFlight.aero and Aviation International News and was previously the Editor for Spaceflight and Astronomy news here at Space.com. As an editor with over 10 years of experience in science journalism she has previously written for Scholastic Classroom Magazines, MedPage Today and The Joint Institute for Computational Sciences at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. After studying physics at the University of Tennessee in her hometown of Knoxville, she earned her graduate degree in Science, Health and Environmental Reporting (SHERP) from New York University. Hanneke joined the Space.com team in 2016 as a staff writer and producer, covering topics including spaceflight and astronomy. She currently lives in Seattle, home of the Space Needle, with her cat and two snakes. In her spare time, Hanneke enjoys exploring the Rocky Mountains, basking in nature and looking for dark skies to gaze at the cosmos.
paras.zh: Hanneke Weitering 是西北太平洋地区的一名多媒体记者，在 FutureFlight.aero 和 Aviation International News 报道航空业的未来，此前曾担任 Space.com 的航天和天文学新闻编辑。作为一名拥有 10 多年科学新闻经验的编辑，她曾为学术课堂杂志、MedPage Today 和橡树岭国家实验室计算科学研究所撰写文章。在家乡诺克斯维尔的田纳西大学学习物理学后，她在纽约大学获得了科学、健康和环境报告 (SHERP) 研究生学位。 Hanneke 于 2016 年加入 Space.com 团队，担任专职撰稿人和制作人，涵盖航天和天文学等主题。她目前与她的猫和两条蛇住在太空针塔所在地西雅图。在业余时间，汉内克喜欢探索落基山脉，沐浴在大自然中，寻找黑暗的天空凝视宇宙。

articles.title: This Week In Space podcast: Episode 235 — Robots in Dark and Scary Places
articles.author: Space.com Staff

paras.en: On Episode 235 of This Week In Space, Tariq Malik and Rod Pyle are joined by Dr. Jim Green to talk about the past, present, and future of planetary exploration.
paras.zh: 在《本周太空》第 235 集中，塔里克·马利克和罗德·派尔与吉姆·格林博士一起谈论行星探索的过去、现在和未来。

paras.en: Robots have, and always will, be the first to go to the dark and scary places in space. For many years, Jim oversaw these missions for NASA as their Chief Scientist. He has always been passionate about NASA's science programs and believes we're quite likely to find life off-Earth in the near future. Join us!
paras.zh: 机器人已经并将永远成为第一个前往太空中黑暗和可怕的地方的人。多年来，吉姆作为美国宇航局首席科学家监督这些任务。他一直对美国宇航局的科学项目充满热情，并相信我们很可能在不久的将来发现地外生命。加入我们！

paras.en: Get episodes ad-free with Club TWiT at https://twit.tv/clubtwit
paras.zh: 通过 Club TWiT 获取无广告的剧集：https://twit.tv/clubtwit

paras.en: Finally, did you know you can launch your own SpaceX rocket? Model rocket maker Estes' stunning scale model of a Falcon 9 rocket that you can pick up now. The launchable model is a detailed recreation of the Falcon 9 and retails for $149.99. You can save 10% by using the code IN-COLLECTSPACE at checkout, courtesy of our partners collectSPACE.com.
paras.zh: 最后，您知道您可以发射自己的 SpaceX 火箭吗？火箭模型制造商 Estes 制作的令人惊叹的猎鹰 9 号火箭比例模型，您现在就可以购买。该可发射模型是 Falcon 9 的详细重现，零售价为 149.99 美元。您可以在结帐时使用代码 IN-COLLECTSPACE 节省 10%，这是由我们的合作伙伴collectSPACE.com 提供的。

paras.en: This Week in Space covers the new space age. Every Friday we take a deep dive into a fascinating topic. What's happening with the new race to the moon and other planets? When will SpaceX really send people to Mars?
paras.zh: 本周太空周涵盖了新太空时代。每个星期五我们都会深入探讨一个有趣的话题。新一轮的月球和其他行星竞赛发生了什么？ SpaceX什么时候才能真正把人送上火星？

paras.en: Rod Pyle is an author, journalist, television producer and Editor-in-Chief of Ad Astra magazine. He has written 18 books on space history, exploration, and development, including Space 2.0, Innovation the NASA Way, Interplanetary Robots, Blueprint for a Battlestar, Amazing Stories of the Space Age, First On the Moon, and Destination Mars
paras.zh: 罗德·派尔 (Rod Pyle) 是一位作家、记者、电视制片人和《Ad Astra》杂志的主编。他撰写了 18 本有关太空历史、探索和发展的书籍，包括《Space 2.0》、《Innovation the NASA Way》、《Interplanetary Robots》、《Battlestar 蓝图》、《Amazing Stories of the Space Age》、《First On the Moon》和《Destination Mars》

paras.en: In a previous life, Rod produced numerous documentaries and short films for The History Channel, Discovery Communications, and Disney. He also worked in visual effects on Star Trek: Deep Space Nine and the Battlestar Galactica reboot, as well as various sci-fi TV pilots. His most recent TV credit was with the NatGeo documentary on Tom Wolfe's iconic book The Right Stuff.
paras.zh: 罗德曾为历史频道、探索传播公司和迪士尼制作了大量纪录片和短片。他还参与了《星际迷航：深空九号》和《太空堡垒卡拉狄加》重启以及各种科幻电视试播集的视觉效果工作。他最近的电视作品是在国家地理频道 (NatGeo) 纪录片中拍摄的，该纪录片讲述了汤姆·沃尔夫 (Tom Wolfe) 的标志性著作《The Right Stuff》。

paras.en: Responsible for Space.com's editorial vision, Tariq Malik has been the Editor-in-Chief of Space.com since 2019 and has covered space news and science for 18 years. He joined the Space.com team in 2001, first as an intern and soon after as a full-time spaceflight reporter covering human spaceflight, exploration, astronomy and the night sky. He became Space.com's managing editor in 2009. As on-air talent has presented space stories on CNN, Fox News, NPR and others.
paras.zh: Tariq Malik 负责 Space.com 的编辑愿景，自 2019 年起担任 Space.com 的主编，报道太空新闻和科学已有 18 年。他于 2001 年加入 Space.com 团队，首先作为实习生，不久之后成为全职航天记者，报道载人航天、探索、天文学和夜空。 2009 年，他成为 Space.com 的总编辑。作为播音人才，他曾在 CNN、福克斯新闻、NPR 等媒体上讲述太空故事。

paras.en: Tariq is an Eagle Scout (yes, he earned the Space Exploration merit badge), a Space Camp veteran (4 times as a kid, once as an adult), and has taken the ultimate "vomit comet" ride while reporting on zero-gravity fires. Before joining Space.com, he served as a staff reporter for The Los Angeles Times covering city and education beats. He has journalism degrees from the University of Southern California and New York University.
paras.zh: 塔里克是一名鹰级童子军（是的，他获得了太空探索奖章），一名太空营老兵（小时候四次，成年一次），并在报道零重力火灾时乘坐了终极“呕吐彗星”。在加入 Space.com 之前，他曾担任《洛杉矶时报》的特约记者，报道城市和教育动态。他拥有南加州大学和纽约大学的新闻学学位。

paras.en: Space.com is the premier source of space exploration, innovation and astronomy news, chronicling (and celebrating) humanity's ongoing expansion across the final frontier. Originally founded in 1999, Space.com is, and always has been, the passion of writers and editors who are space fans and also trained journalists. Our current news team consists of Editor-in-Chief Tariq Malik; Editor Hanneke Weitering, Senior Space Writer Mike Wall; Senior Writer Meghan Bartels; Senior Writer Chelsea Gohd, Senior Writer Tereza Pultarova and Staff Writer Alexander Cox, focusing on e-commerce. Senior Producer Steve Spaleta oversees our space videos, with Diana Whitcroft as our Social Media Editor.
paras.zh: Space.com 是太空探索、创新和天文学新闻的主要来源，记录（并庆祝）人类在最后疆域的持续扩张。 Space.com 最初成立于 1999 年，一直以来都是太空迷作家和编辑以及训练有素的记者的热情所在。我们目前的新闻团队由主编塔里克·马利克 (Tariq Malik) 组成；编辑 Hanneke Weitering、高级空间作家 Mike Wall；资深作家梅根·巴特尔斯；高级作家 Chelsea Gohd、高级作家 Tereza Pultarova 和特约作家 Alexander Cox，专注于电子商务。高级制作人 Steve Spaleta 负责监督我们的太空视频，Diana Whitcroft 担任我们的社交媒体编辑。
